MOGG · call conformance and outlining

Move the routine body into a named helper, preserve its caller, and simplify the code generation operations before runtime lowering.

Fused attention: Q/K/V = float32[32,32], gpu:0; BN=16, BD=8. Blue blocks show concrete states and transformations. IR names and simplified syntax are schematic. TEST labels identify inspected repository expectations, not tests run for this example.

QnA 1 · What work happens in the MOGG stage?

MOGG turns the implementation body into a well-formed callable helper. This stage conforms call operands, outlines the routine body, adds a trace region and cleans up the resulting module. The tensor-level mogg.routine container remains for runtime lowering. ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:370 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:14

QnA 2 · Does ConformCallOperands change Q, K, V or the output here?

The registered signature uses three ordinary InputTensor arguments, one ordinary OutputTensor, and one DeviceContext. It does not request scalar, variadic or trait-bound tensor arguments. The existing ordinary tensor operands therefore pass through this packing step. ↗ fused_attention.mojo:82 ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:134

packCall copies the declaration's function adaptor before changing output contracts; it does not rewrite P1's registered API. The SSA call is replaced only when conformance changes something. Outlining subsequently moves its body objects into a helper and creates new forwarding objects in the graph-local routine. ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:270 ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:305 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:109 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:124

Attention call before conformance
  inputs  = [%Q,%K,%V]       all ordinary read-only tensor views
  outputs = [%O]            ordinary writable output view
  context = [%ctx]          single device context
  params  = {BD=8, BN=16}

Attention call after conformance
  inputs  = [%Q,%K,%V]
  outputs = [%O]
  context = [%ctx]
  params  = {BD=8, BN=16}

The pass still checks the declaration mapping. When no packing or overload adjustment is needed, it returns without replacing the call. Existing types and shape metadata remain available to the subsequent emitter. ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:259 ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:305

The implementation also has an unfused-overload path for eligible fused-output kernels. This attention output is already ordinary, so no pass-through epilogue needs removal here. ↗ ConformCallOperands.cpp:273 ↗ fused_attention.mojo:82

QnA 3 · Show exactly what outlining moves and what it leaves behind.

Outlining creates a named function from an existing region body. For readability, @F_attention below names the new helper; the real symbol is derived from fusion provenance and uniqued by the module symbol table. ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:83 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:105

BEFORE · one graph-local routine body
IR1 : builtin.module
└─ mo.graph @fused_attention
   └─ mogg.routine(%q,%k,%v) → %o:T0
      └─ body(%qptr,%kptr,%vptr,%optr,%ctx)
         ├─ shape/tensor constructors
         └─ mogg.call.opaque → P1.FusedAttention

AFTER · tensor boundary and helper are separate
IR1 : builtin.module
├─ mo.graph @fused_attention
│  └─ mogg.routine(%q,%k,%v) → %o:T0
│     └─ NEW body(%qptr,%kptr,%vptr,%optr,%ctx)
│        └─ mogg.call @F_attention(%qptr,%kptr,%vptr,%optr,%ctx)
└─ mogg.func @F_attention          abi=MOGG, device="gpu"
   └─ MOVED body(%qptr,%kptr,%vptr,%optr,%ctx)
      ├─ shape/tensor constructors
      ├─ mogg.call.opaque → P1.FusedAttention
      └─ mogg.output              no by-value tensor return

The implementation literally transfers the body using takeBody. It then creates fresh arguments for the retained routine's forwarding call. This move changes ownership of IR blocks; it does not copy Q/K/V data. ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:109 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:124

F_attention signature
  (!mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer,
   !mogg.pointer, !mogg.context) → ()

Meaning
  Q pointer, K pointer, V pointer, O pointer, GPU context
  O is written through its pointer; no tensor object is returned by this helper.

Enclosing routine signature remains (T0,T0,T0) → T0.
G1's original Python graph remains separate from all these IR1 objects.

The source obtains the helper's signature from the routine body's argument types. For an ordinary output tensor, it adds no by-value return. The actual kernel implementation also puts its OutputTensor in the argument list. ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:49 ↗ OutlineRoutines.cpp:65 ↗ fused_attention.mojo:82

QnA 4 · How do tracing, canonicalization and CSE transform the helper?

Trace wrapping leaves setup before the first call outside the trace and moves the operations from that call onward into a mogg.with_trace region. This records an instrumentation boundary; it is not a GPU execution event during compilation. ↗ WrapFuncsWithTrace.cpp:44 ↗ WrapFuncsWithTrace.cpp:65

BEFORE tracing
  shape/tensor setup
  call FusedAttention
  mogg.output

AFTER tracing
  shape/tensor setup
  mogg.with_trace {
    call FusedAttention
    mogg.yield
  }
  mogg.output

For the static attention body, four calls to buildShape([32,32]) initially create equivalent shape descriptions. CSE can share their eligible shape-producing operations. The Q/K/V/O tensor views remain distinct because they reference different pointers and output mutability differs. ↗ MAPOpsLowerableToMOGG.cpp:102 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:378

BEFORE cleanup                         AFTER eligible CSE
  sq = shape.create([32,32])              s = shape.create([32,32])
  sk = shape.create([32,32])              Q = tensor(qptr,s,Input,false)
  sv = shape.create([32,32])              K = tensor(kptr,s,Input,false)
  so = shape.create([32,32])              V = tensor(vptr,s,Input,false)
  Q = tensor(qptr,sq,Input,false)         O = tensor(optr,s,Output,true)
  K = tensor(kptr,sk,Input,false)
  V = tensor(vptr,sv,Input,false)
  O = tensor(optr,so,Output,true)

Illustration of an eligible cleanup, not a captured dump.
Shared shape description ≠ shared tensor storage.

Identical computation with side effects is not automatically redundant. In particular, later mogg.compiled.call operations may read/write their pointed-to buffers, so unused results or equal operands do not authorize erasing those calls. ↗ MOGGOps.td:444

The generated code later converts the scalar tensor through the registered scalar primitive. Tuple packing describes a call argument aggregate; it does not imply concatenation of the tensor elements. ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1944 ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:1960

QnA 6 · What reaches MOGG→MGP?

IR1
├─ mo.graph @fused_attention : (T0,T0,T0) → T0
│  ├─ one mogg.routine with device=gpu:0
│  │  └─ call @F_attention through 4 pointers + context
│  └─ mo.output %o
└─ mogg.func @F_attention
   ├─ ABI = MOGG
   ├─ device kind = "gpu"
   ├─ tensor construction from [32,32], f32
   └─ registered implementation call, BN=16, BD=8

No GPU binary or initialized Model has been produced at this boundary.
Next: map tensors to storage and build the runtime model's two regions.

MOGG→MGP consumes the retained routine and its outlined helper. Later EmitMojo writes helper source, and JIT compilation turns that source and P1 implementations into native artifacts. Keeping those steps separate explains why creating @F_attention is not yet machine-code generation. ↗ MOGGOps.cpp:716 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:611 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:484 ↗ GraphCompiler.cpp:619

QnA 7 · How do operand conformance, outlining, tracing and rowwise legalization change concrete calls while retaining their data and ownership contracts?

SOURCE · nine worked examples. The IR diagrams are schematic, with shortened symbols and attribute spellings. Numeric inputs are illustrative; no MAX, Mojo, GPU or compiler-test workload was executed. TEST paragraphs explain where independently supplied .mlir inputs enter a test pipeline and what the CHECK directives expect. The production compiler does not call these files. A test that checks emitted source establishes an emission expectation, not a measured numerical result.

Example 1 · Why is attention's call unchanged by packing, yet moved into a new named helper by outlining?

The actual attention call has three ordinary InputTensor operands Q/K/V, one ordinary OutputTensor O, and one DeviceContext. Each tensor is f32[32,32]; BN=16,BD=8 remain call parameters. With the illustrative inputs Q=K=0 and V[j,d]=j, O still represents 32 rows filled with 15.5. Conformance and outlining modify the calling structure around that same computation. ↗ fused_attention.mojo:74 ↗ fused_attention.mojo:82 ↗ fused_attention.py:57

BEFORE · schematic MOGG inside IR1
mo.graph @fused_attention(%q,%k,%v) -> T0 {             # Retain the graph's tensor boundary.
  %o = mogg.routine(%q,%k,%v) -> T0 {             # Bind the future output destination.
    OLD body(%qp,%kp,%vp,%op:pointer,%ctx:context) # Five existing body arguments.
    shape/tensor constructors → %Q,%K,%V,%O       # Rebuild four typed tensor views.
    call.opaque @FusedAttention                   # Same P1 implementation.
      inputs(%Q,%K,%V) outputs(%O) context(%ctx)   # Ordinary signature already matches.
      params={BN=16,BD=8}                        # Tile parameters stay compile-time data.
  }
  mo.output %o                                   # Return one graph tensor.
}

packAgainstSignature still maps those operands to the declaration, but packOperands returns each ordinary tensor directly. No scalar, tuple, trait or mutable-input repair is needed; the final guard keeps the existing CallOpaqueOp object. ConformCallOperands.cpp:134 ConformCallOperands.cpp:279

if (!changed)
  return success();

Outlining then creates a module-level mogg.func, derives its parameter types from the routine body, registers its name and moves the body into it. This is the central ownership operation. OutlineRoutines.cpp:95 OutlineRoutines.cpp:109

stub.getBody().takeBody(kernel.getBody());
Block &stubBody = stub.getBody().front();
AFTER · schematic MOGG before tracing
mo.graph @fused_attention(%q,%k,%v) -> T0 {             # Original tensor contract remains.
  %o = mogg.routine(%q,%k,%v) -> T0 {             # Same routine operation and outer uses.
    NEW body(%qp2,%kp2,%vp2,%op2:pointer,%ctx2)    # Fresh forwarding arguments.
    mogg.call @F_attention(%qp2,%kp2,%vp2,%op2,%ctx2) # Forward all five references.
  }
  mo.output %o                                   # Same graph result.
}
mogg.func @F_attention abi=MOGG device="gpu" {    # New module sibling of the graph.
  MOVED body(%qp,%kp,%vp,%op:pointer,%ctx)        # Existing block and arguments move here.
  shape/tensor constructors → %Q,%K,%V,%O         # Existing setup operations move with it.
  call.opaque @FusedAttention                     # Existing call object moves with the block.
    inputs(%Q,%K,%V) outputs(%O) context(%ctx)     # Same operand identities within that block.
    params={BN=16,BD=8}                          # Same parameters.
  mogg.output                                    # No by-value result for this tensor output.
}
Object Conformance Outlining
P1 declaration read for matching retained
CallOpaqueOp in attention retained unchanged moved with its block
routine's original block/arguments retained owned by new helper
routine's replacement block/call absent newly created
Q/K/V/O payload buffers not evaluated by this pass future pointers are forwarded
G1's Python graph separate from IR1 separate from IR1

@F_attention is a teaching name. The implementation derives a preferred name from fusion provenance, then symtab.insert(stub) returns a unique symbol when names collide. The new call uses that returned symbol. Two routines with the same preferred name are not merged by this outlining pass. OutlineRoutines.cpp:83 OutlineRoutines.cpp:105 OutlineRoutines.cpp:133

Its plain [2,2] case checks that the graph-local body contains mogg.call, that mogg.call.opaque appears inside the new private helper, and that the helper has abi=MOGG and a terminator. Its dynamic case checks pointer, pointer, dimension, context in the forwarded argument list and helper signature. Example 2 · How does a rank-zero tensor carrying 5 become a scalar call operand without evaluating the kernel?

Use the test signature (output: OutputTensor, a: InputTensor, s: Scalar[dtype], ctx). Choose a:[4]=[1,2,3,4] and a rank-zero f32 tensor s:[] containing 5.0. The packing pass changes the representation of s at the call boundary. The fixture's kernel body is empty, so no result such as a+5 is implied. codegen-map-abi-stub.mlir:51 testing_kernels.mojo:3713

BEFORE · schematic MOGG
%A = tensor.create(%ap,shape=[4],f32,Input,false)  # Four data elements in the ordinary input.
%S = tensor.create(%sp,shape=[],f32,Input,false)   # One scalar value, rank zero.
%O = tensor.create(%op,shape=[4],f32,Output,true)  # Preserve the output destination.
call.opaque @MapLowerScalar inputs(%A,%S) outputs(%O) context(%ctx) # S is still a tensor view.

Operand inference identifies the second input as a scalar parameter. packOperands creates one ScalarCreateOp, sets changed=true, and advances to the next input. ConformCallOperands.cpp:83

if (arg.isScalarType()) {
  packed.push_back(ScalarCreateOp::create(
      builder, loc, ScalarType::get(ctx), operands[i]));
  changed = true;
  ++i;
  continue;
}
AFTER · schematic MOGG
%A,%S,%O retain their existing producers           # No tensor contents change here.
%scalar = mogg.scalar.create(%S)                   # New scalar representation of S's payload.
call.opaque @MapLowerScalar                        # New call operation, same callee.
  inputs(%A,%scalar) outputs(%O) context(%ctx)      # Only the second input changes representation.

The old call is erased after replacement. Its callee, parameters, result types and epilogue-fusion flag are retained. Later ScalarCreateOp::emitMojo emits a call to the registered mogg.as_scalar primitive; conformance itself only builds an IR operation and does not read %sp. ConformCallOperands.cpp:311 ScalarCreateOp::emitMojo:1944

Candidate original MO operand Signature check
immutable tensor<[],f32> on CPU scalar-compatible
immutable tensor<[1],f32> on CPU rank 1; rejected as a scalar argument
rank-zero tensor on GPU rejected by the host-scalar requirement
already lowered !mogg.tensor rank/device metadata is no longer in this handle type; upstream validation supplies that contract

The rank and host-device checks occur in matchConvertedMOTypeToKernelDeclType. At the MOGG boundary the same helper recognizes an opaque codegen handle whose rank/device were checked earlier; it does not infer rank zero from the number of tensor handles. OperandInference.cpp:81

The test bypasses MO→MAP/MAP→MOGG deliberately to isolate this packing rule. package.mlir:10

Its scalar checks require the emitted mogg_as_scalar result to be passed to MapLowerScalar.execute. It reads generated source using FileCheck; it does not execute that kernel. The abbreviated pipeline uses -verify-each=false because it stops after emission erases the helper while the routine still names it. codegen-map-abi-stub.mlir:15 codegen-map-abi-stub.mlir:45

Example 3 · How are several tensor operands packed into one variadic argument while preserving their separate buffers?

Use two immutable input views A:[4]=[1,2,3,4] and B:[4]=[10,20,30,40], with a signature declaring one InputVariadicTensors parameter. The flat call has two tensor operands; the declaration says both belong to the same parameter. Their numerical contents remain separate. This fixture has an empty body, so its output computation is unspecified. testing_kernels.mojo:3728

BEFORE · schematic MOGG
call.opaque @MapLowerVariadic                     # Declaration expects one tensor aggregate.
  inputs(%A,%B) outputs(%O) context(%ctx)          # Flat input list still has two handles.

OPERAND MAPPING
flat input 0 → declaration position "inputs"      # First member of this variadic run.
flat input 1 → declaration position "inputs"      # Same declared position, same run.

packOperands records the declaration position and collects consecutive operands only while their mapping refers to that same variadic parameter. It then creates one tuple operation. This is the native run-boundary check. ConformCallOperands.cpp:91

unsigned pos = arg.sourceDescriptor->position;
SmallVector<Value> run;
while (i < e) {
  auto runIt = mapping.find(i);
  if (runIt == mapping.end() || !runIt->second.isVariadicTensorType() ||
      runIt->second.sourceDescriptor->position != pos)
    break;
  run.push_back(operands[i]);
  ++i;
}
AFTER · schematic MOGG
%inputs = mogg.tuple.create(%A,%B) variadic_abi=plain # Aggregate two existing references.
call.opaque @MapLowerVariadic                       # Rebuild the call with the same symbol.
  inputs(%inputs) outputs(%O) context(%ctx)          # One aggregate input, same output/context.

Logical aggregate
member 0 → A pointer + shape [4] → [1,2,3,4]       # Retain A's storage identity.
member 1 → B pointer + shape [4] → [10,20,30,40]   # Retain B's storage identity.

The later emitter builds runtime pointer/shape tuples and compile-time tensor specifications. There is no concatenation of the eight input elements in this packing operation. A real mo.concat still performs its declared concatenation through its implementation; packing only prepares the argument aggregate it receives. MOGGOps.cpp:1963

Declared parameter kind Tuple's recorded ABI Information retained
ordinary variadic tensors plain per-member data references and shapes
stable variadic tensors stable slot-backed member convention
fused input/output variadics fused_input / fused_output member fusion convention
trait TensorTuple tensor_tuple per-member trait adapters; worked in Example 4

The choice comes from the declaration's adaptor, not from guessing based on a producer's mutability. ConformCallOperands.cpp:108

Guard against ambiguous groups. If one input list binds multiple variadic parameters, operand inference requires hasSameVariadicOperandSize; otherwise the flat list supplies no group boundaries. Launch arguments such as the context are skipped during this tensor mapping. OperandInference.cpp:116 OperandInference.cpp:166

Their order comes from the earlier MAP→MOGG unique-device collection. Ordinary attention declares one context and skips this branch. ConformCallOperands.cpp:290 MAPOpsLowerableToMOGG.cpp:966

Example 4 · How do ordinary and heterogeneous tensor arguments acquire the declared trait contracts?

TraitNegate declares input/output arguments through TileTensorable traits. For illustrative X:[4]=[1,-2,3,-4], its body writes O=[-1,2,-3,4]. Conformance prepares the trait-compatible argument representation while preserving these element and storage roles. testing_kernels.mojo:328 testing_kernels.mojo:351

BEFORE · schematic MOGG
%X = tensor.create(%xp,[4],f32,Input,false)       # Plain read-only tensor view.
%O = tensor.create(%op,[4],f32,Output,true)       # Plain writable tensor view.
call.opaque @TraitNegate inputs(%X) outputs(%O) context(%ctx) # Declaration requests trait arguments.

AFTER · schematic MOGG
%Xarg = mogg.trait.create(%X)                     # New input adapter over the same view.
  contract={role=input,fused=false,access=none,capabilities=none}, device="cpu"
%Oarg = mogg.trait.create(%O)                     # New output adapter over the same destination.
  contract={role=output,fused=false,access=none,capabilities=none}, device="cpu"
call.opaque @TraitNegate inputs(%Xarg) outputs(%Oarg) context(%ctx) # Same negation computation.

The helper asTraitArg skips already-fused contracts, otherwise builds TraitCreateOp using the operand's own MOGG kind and the enclosing routine's device label. A mutable input can remain !mogg.buffer; ordinary input/output tensors remain !mogg.tensor. The adapter's IR type alone is therefore insufficient to explain the contract—the attribute carries that information. ConformCallOperands.cpp:61

if (contract.fused)
  return operand;
changed = true;
// Keep the operand's own kind: a mutable-input trait argument comes in as
// a `!mogg.buffer`, everything else as a `!mogg.tensor`.
return TraitCreateOp::create(builder, loc, operand.getType(), operand,
                             builder.getStringAttr(device.getLabel()),
                             tensorArgContractToAttr(ctx, contract));

The original input/output tensor constructors retain their respective mut=false/true attributes. conform-trait-args.mlir:15

Heterogeneous members keep their own shapes and dtypes. The TraitTensorTupleAdd test supplies bias f32[1], A si32[2], B f64[3], with outputs f32[2] and si32[3]. Choose illustrative bias [10], A [1,2], B [3,4,5]; the registered body casts each member to its corresponding output dtype and adds the bias, yielding [11,12] and [13,14,15]. conform-trait-tensor-tuple.mlir:42 testing_kernels.mojo:871

BEFORE · flat call lists

AFTER · schematic trait and tuple packing
%barg = trait.create(%bias,role=input)            # Ordinary bias parameter remains separate.
%aarg = trait.create(%A,role=input)               # Preserve A's si32[2] contract.
%bmember = trait.create(%B,role=input)            # Preserve B's f64[3] contract.
%ins = tuple.create(%aarg,%bmember) abi=tensor_tuple # One heterogeneous input aggregate.
%o0arg = trait.create(%O0,role=output)             # Preserve O0's f32[2] destination.
%o1arg = trait.create(%O1,role=output)             # Preserve O1's si32[3] destination.
%outs = tuple.create(%o0arg,%o1arg) abi=tensor_tuple # One heterogeneous output aggregate.
call @TraitTensorTupleAdd inputs(%barg,%ins) outputs(%outs) # Same paired computations.

This adds five trait adapters and two tuples; the routine's three input pointers, two output pointers and context stay as its boundary arguments. In the variadic branch, the compiler applies asTraitArg to each member before constructing the tensor_tuple aggregate. ConformCallOperands.cpp:109

Example 5 · How can a read-only kernel argument use a mutable buffer without changing the destination's write permission?

The test's graph has distinct dst and srcbuf, both f32[2,2]. MAP fusion has absorbed a mutable load of srcbuf into a call whose dst parameter is mutable and whose src parameter is read-only. MAP→MOGG initially reconstructs both buffer inputs as mutable !mogg.buffer views. fused-mutable-load-opaque.mlir:8

BEFORE · schematic MOGG after MAP→MOGG
%D = tensor.create(%dstp,[2,2],f32,Input,true) : buffer # Kernel is allowed to write dst.
%Smut = tensor.create(%srcp,[2,2],f32,Input,true) : buffer # Storage originally arrived as a buffer.
call @MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%D,%Smut) context(%ctx) # Second parameter only reads.

Outer routine keeps its dependency chain and read/write effects. # Preserve ordering of buffer access.

packAgainstSignature enables mutable-to-immutable input matching for opaque kernel calls. For a mapped non-mutable parameter, it requires a !mogg.buffer operand whose producer implements TensorCreateInterface and is marked mutable. It clones that producer with mut=false and rewires just this call input. ConformCallOperands.cpp:170

Value operand = reconciledInputs[idx];
if (!isa<BufferType>(operand.getType()))
  continue;
auto producer = operand.getDefiningOp<TensorCreateInterface>();
if (!producer || !producer.getMut())
  continue;
builder.setInsertionPointAfter(producer);
reconciledInputs[idx] =
    producer.cloneWithMut(builder, /*mut=*/false)->getResult(0);
reconciled = true;
AFTER · schematic MOGG immediately after conformance
%D = tensor.create(%dstp,[2,2],f32,Input,true) : buffer # Retain the mutable destination view.
%Smut = tensor.create(%srcp,[2,2],f32,Input,true) : buffer # Old view may become dead.
%Sread = tensor.create(%srcp,[2,2],f32,Input,false) : tensor # New read-only view, same pointer.
call @MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%D,%Sread) context(%ctx) # Match each parameter independently.

Later cleanup may erase %Smut if no users remain.       # Producer cleanup does not free src storage.

For illustrative source contents [[1,2],[3,4]], %Sread still refers to those same four f32 elements; it describes 16 payload bytes beginning at the same symbolic %srcp. The compiler neither copies them nor makes dst immutable. This signature-only testing kernel has an empty body, so the example deliberately makes no claim about values written to dst. testing_kernels.mojo:3616

Guard Action
parameter is actually mutable keep %D as a buffer
argument is already an ordinary immutable tensor keep it
read-only parameter, mutable tensor-creation producer clone producer with mut=false and replace this use
immutable value proposed for a mutable output no reverse widening; signature mismatch remains an error

Input matching permits only the mutable-buffer-to-read-only-view conversion. Output matching calls the same matcher with allowMutToImmut=false. Existing dependency chains continue to order access to the original storage. OperandInference.cpp:57 OperandInference.cpp:322

Example 6 · When can pass-through output epilogues be removed to select an unfused execute overload?

A kernel can advertise both a fused-output execute and an ordinary-output overload. Suppose its result must be written unchanged to each destination: the output epilogues only forward (value,index) to a captured output. Passing the ordinary output views directly can express that same destination behavior. packCall attempts this only when the declaration advertises the overload and the call-wide hasEpilogueFusion flag is false. ConformCallOperands.cpp:270

bool selectedUnfused = adaptor.supportsUnfusedExecute &&
                       !call.getHasEpilogueFusion() &&
                       selectUnfusedExecute(fn, outputs, droppedEpilogues);
BEFORE · schematic two-output call with pass-through epilogues
%ez = tensor.create.epilogue(%v,%i) captures(%Z) { # One destination capture.
  tensor.store %Z[%i] = %v                        # Write the supplied value unchanged.
}
%ew = tensor.create.epilogue(%v,%i) captures(%W) { # Second independent destination.
  tensor.store %W[%i] = %v                        # Another pass-through store.
}
call @K inputs(%X) outputs(%ez,%ew)               # Same kernel symbol has two execute forms.
  hasEpilogueFusion=false                         # No output arithmetic was fused.

selectUnfusedExecute inspects every fused output before mutating the output list. Each must be a TensorCreateEpilogueOp, have one use, and not recompute the value. Any failure keeps the fused form for the whole call. ConformCallOperands.cpp:237

auto epilogue = dyn_cast<TensorCreateEpilogueOp>(producer.getOperation());
if (!epilogue || !out.hasOneUse() || epilogue.recomputesValue())
  return false;
passThroughs.emplace_back(i, epilogue);

The producer's recomputesValue() uses a strict pass-through test: the body must contain exactly one operation, either a yield of the incoming value or a store of that value at the incoming index into the first capture. Even unchanged data with extra index-transform operations does not satisfy that simple-body test. MOGGOps.cpp:3439

On success, the output operand becomes the epilogue's first capture, its store target. The compiler strips fusion from the local copy of each output contract and packs those ordinary outputs. The registered declaration is retained. ConformCallOperands.cpp:249

AFTER · schematic successful selection
%Xarg = trait.create(%X,ordinary-input-contract)   # Adapt the unchanged input if trait-bound.
%Zarg = trait.create(%Z,ordinary-output-contract)  # Wrap the original Z destination if trait-bound.
%Warg = trait.create(%W,ordinary-output-contract)  # Wrap the original W destination if trait-bound.
call @K inputs(%Xarg) outputs(%Zarg,%Warg)         # Same callee symbol; plain operand types choose overload.
remove %ez and %ew                                # Drop the two pass-through regions.
remove their unused pure pointer/setup producers # Erase only when no live use remains.

Value-preserving illustration for an overload pair with equal contracts
X=[1,2,3,4], Z=X+1, W=X-1                         # Both overloads implement these same expressions.
Z=[2,3,4,5], W=[0,1,2,3] before and after          # Only destination passing changes.

The arithmetic pair above is a teaching contract for equivalent overloads. The repository's test kernel deliberately adds a diagnostic output, discussed below. The cleanup only erases an epilogue operand's defining operation when it has no uses and is memory-effect-free. It does not erase the tensor storage behind a surviving output view. ConformCallOperands.cpp:320

SKIPPED · one output actually transforms the value
%ew = tensor.create.epilogue(%v,%i) captures(%W,%X) { # Fuse work into the W output.
  %x = tensor.load %X[%i]                            # Read X at the same element.
  %sum = call.elementwise @Add(%v,%x)               # Change the value to store.
  tensor.store %W[%i] = %sum                        # Preserve the fused addition.
}
call @K outputs(%ez,%ew) hasEpilogueFusion=true      # Keep both outputs in fused form.
Condition Outcome
advertised overload + all fused outputs are private pass-throughs replace those epilogues by ordinary destinations
any output recomputes a value keep the fused call
a fused output has another user keep the fused call
a fused output is a different producer kind keep the fused call
no output epilogues are present selector returns false; nothing to remove

Example 7 · Why does outlining move a constant's pointer back to the call site and add a helper argument for it?

Consider a routine that copies a constant matrix C=[[1,2],[3,4]] into its f32[2,2] output. The routine has no tensor inputs. MAP→MOGG has created mogg.buffer.constant for the embedded bytes and an input view over that pointer. Its output remains a distinct destination. ConstantOp::lowerToMOGG:203

BEFORE · schematic MOGG routine
%o = mogg.routine() -> f32[2,2] {                 # Graph has no user tensor inputs.
  body(%op:pointer,%ctx:context)                  # Output destination and context only.
  %osh = shape.create([2,2])                      # Describe the output dimensions.
  %O = tensor.create(%op,%osh,f32,Output,true)     # Writable output view.
  %cp = mogg.buffer.constant [1,2,3,4] : f32[2,2] # Embedded payload's pointer-producing op.
  %csh = shape.create([2,2])                      # Describe the constant dimensions.
  %C = tensor.create(%cp,%csh,f32,Input,false)     # Read-only constant view.
  %lsh = shape.create([2,2])                      # Describe the loop dimensions.
  call.foreach shape(%lsh) captures(%C,%O) {      # Copy the four logical elements later.
    %v = tensor.load %cArg[%i]                    # Read the constant at the loop index.
    tensor.store %oArg[%i] = %v                  # Store the same value to output.
  }
}

outlineKernel collects nested BufferConstantOps and adds one trailing !mogg.pointer to the helper signature for each constant. Resources later enter through the runtime-facing MGP ABI; the pointer-based MOGG helper does not have that resource table. OutlineRoutines.cpp:55

SmallVector<MOGG::BufferConstantOp> constants;
body.walk([&](MOGG::BufferConstantOp cst) { constants.push_back(cst); });

SmallVector<Type> stubArgTypes(argTypes);
stubArgTypes.append(constants.size(), MOGG::PointerType::get(ctx));

After takeBody, it rewires uses of each constant pointer inside the moved body to the newly added helper argument. It then moves the constant operation itself back into the routine's new call-site block and forwards its pointer. OutlineRoutines.cpp:114 OutlineRoutines.cpp:129

for (MOGG::BufferConstantOp cst : constants)
  cst.getPointer().replaceAllUsesWith(
      stubBody.addArgument(MOGG::PointerType::get(ctx), cst.getLoc()));
AFTER · schematic MOGG
%o = mogg.routine() -> f32[2,2] {                  # Still no user tensor input.
  NEW body(%op2:pointer,%ctx2:context)             # Same routine boundary types.
  %cp = mogg.buffer.constant [1,2,3,4] : f32[2,2] # Existing resource operation moved back here.
  mogg.call @F_copy(%op2,%ctx2,%cp)                # Constant pointer is a trailing helper argument.
}
mogg.func @F_copy(%op:pointer,%ctx:context,%cArg:pointer) { # New three-argument helper.
  MOVED %osh = shape.create([2,2])                # Output setup moves with the original block.
  MOVED %O = tensor.create(%op,%osh,f32,Output,true) # Same output view.
  MOVED %csh = shape.create([2,2])                 # Constant shape operation also moves.
  MOVED %C = tensor.create(%cArg,%csh,f32,Input,false) # Only pointer operand is redirected.
  MOVED %lsh = shape.create([2,2])                 # Loop domain operation also moves.
  MOVED call.foreach shape(%lsh) captures(%C,%O) { # Same copying computation.
    %v = tensor.load %cView[%i]                   # Still reads 1,2,3,4 from C.
    tensor.store %oView[%i] = %v                 # Future O still becomes [[1,2],[3,4]].
  }
  mogg.output                                     # Tensor output is written through %op.
}

The constant's 16 payload bytes remain embedded data. There is one constant operation at the call site, not a second copied constant in the helper. A helper argument was added; no input was added to the public graph. CPU alignment and runtime constant-buffer materialization belong to later MOGG→MGP work. OutlineRoutines.cpp:55 MAPOpsLowerableToMOGG.cpp:200

Ordinary attention returns no value from its helper because O is written through a pointer. A shape helper instead ends in mogg.output %shapeValue. Outlining obtains helper result types from that terminator's operands, so it can preserve a !mogg.shape_func_result<4> return or an opaque by-value result as well. OutlineRoutines.cpp:65

    dyn_cast<MOGG::OutputOp>(body.empty() ? nullptr : &body.back());
SmallVector<Type> stubResultTypes;
if (bodyOutput)
  llvm::append_range(stubResultTypes, bodyOutput.getOperandTypes());

BEFORE · schematic outlined MOGG helper
func @F_shape(%ip:pointer,%jp:pointer,%ctx:context) -> shape_result<4> {
  %I = tensor.create(%ip,shape=[1,2,3],Input,false) # Initial view construction.
  %J = tensor.create(%jp,shape=[4,5],Input,false)   # Second input view construction.
  %s = call.shape @gather_shape_fn(%I,%J)          # First CallLike operation.
       params={axis=-2,output_rank=4}             # Same shape-function arguments.
  mogg.output %s                                 # Return its dimension tuple by value.
}

WrapFuncsWithTrace skips non-MOGG-ABI functions. For a MOGG helper, it collects operations from the first CallLike onward, excluding the terminator and any existing WithTraceOp. Setup before that first call stays outside; operations after it move with the dispatch. If the collected list is empty, the function is unchanged. WrapFuncsWithTrace.cpp:38 WrapFuncsWithTrace.cpp:48

The new trace operation has result types matching the original terminator operands. mogg.yield forwards those operands from the nested region, and the outer terminator is rewired to the trace results. This unchanged excerpt implements the final forwarding step. WrapFuncsWithTrace.cpp:65

builder.setInsertionPointToEnd(&tracedBlock);
MOGG::YieldOp::create(builder, loc, terminator->getOperands());
terminator->setOperands(withTrace.getOutputs());
AFTER · schematic MOGG helper
func @F_shape(%ip:pointer,%jp:pointer,%ctx:context) -> shape_result<4> {
  %I = tensor.create(%ip,shape=[1,2,3],Input,false) # Same setup before trace boundary.
  %J = tensor.create(%jp,shape=[4,5],Input,false)   # Same setup and input references.
  %traced = mogg.with_trace -> shape_result<4> {   # New result-bearing instrumentation region.
    %s = call.shape @gather_shape_fn(%I,%J)        # Original call moves here.
         params={axis=-2,output_rank=4}           # Same shape computation.
    mogg.yield %s                                # Forward [1,4,5,3] out of the trace.
  }
  mogg.output %traced                             # Forward the same four values to the caller.
}

Example 9 · What does rowwise legalization add to a sum-of-squares reduction, and what malformed bodies does it reject?

This pass runs first in the MOGG stage. Use the test's visible graph Y = reduce_add(cast_f32(X) * cast_f32(X)) + B, with X:bf16[8,128], B:f32[8,1] and Y:f32[8,1]. For an illustrative first row [1,2,3,0,…,0] and bias 5, the required first output is 1+4+9+5=19. Set the other rows and biases to zero to make the remaining seven outputs zero. LegalizeRowwiseKernels/legalize.mlir:19

BEFORE · schematic MOGG after MAP→MOGG
call.rowwise shape=[8,128], axis=1, captures(%X,%B,%O) { # Rowwise body lacks legalization metadata.
  %acc = rowwise.reduce @ReduceSum(%i) -> simd<f32> {   # Fold over one row's 128 elements.
    %x = tensor.load %xArg[%i] -> simd<bf16>            # Read the primary input at the element index.
    %a = call.elementwise @Cast(%x) -> simd<f32>       # Accumulate using f32 values.
    %sq = call.elementwise @Mul(%a,%a)                 # Square each element.
    mogg.yield %sq                                    # Contribute to the sum.
  }
  %b = tensor.load %bArg[%row]                         # Read one bias per row.
  %y = call.elementwise @Add(%acc,%b)                  # Add bias after reduction.
  tensor.store %oArg[%row] = %y                       # Write the row's one output value.
}

The umbrella pass schedules four subpasses in order: select primary input, bind monoids, group row stores, then set launch parameters. selectPrimaryInput chooses the first capture loaded by the first fold at its own element index. It replaces matching loads in all folds with RowwisePrimaryOp and records the capture number and dtype. LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:315 LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:78

auto value =
    RowwisePrimaryOp::create(builder, load.getLoc(), load.getType());
dtype = value.getType().getElementType();
load.replaceAllUsesWith(value.getResult());
load.erase();

Here that selects capture 0, X, with dtype=bf16. One fold reads it, so is_cached remains false. bindMonoid uses ReduceSum's declared output field to record fields=["acc"] and parameter dtype=f32, while the widest yielded contribution type gives the rowwise accumulator dtype f32. LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:113 LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:128 LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:170

AFTER · schematic legalized MOGG
call.rowwise shape=[8,128], axis=1, captures(%X,%B,%O)  # Same tensors and reduction domain.
  attrs={primary=0,dtype=bf16,accum=f32,cols=128,         # Record input/accumulator/extent metadata.
         num_phases=1,dtype_size=0,simd_monoid=@ReduceSum} {
  %acc = rowwise.reduce @ReduceSum(%i) -> simd<f32>       # Same sum operation.
    fields=["acc"], params={dtype=f32} {
    %x = mogg.rowwise.primary -> simd<bf16>              # Read the selected primary stream.
    %a = call.elementwise @Cast(%x) -> simd<f32>         # Same conversion.
    %sq = call.elementwise @Mul(%a,%a)                   # Same square.
    mogg.yield %sq                                      # Same contributions 1,4,9,0,….
  }
  %b = tensor.load %bArg[%row]                           # Same per-row bias.
  %y = call.elementwise @Add(%acc,%b)                    # First illustrative row remains 14+5.
  mogg.rowwise.emit {                                    # New region groups row-result writes.
    tensor.store %oArg[%row] = %y                       # Existing store moves into this region.
  }
}

groupRowStores moves stores whose index is the row argument into one RowwiseEmitOp; it does not change their values or create an output buffer. setLaunchParams then rejects any store outside such an emit region, sets the supported reduction phase metadata, and reads the known axis extent to set cols=128. The cost flag is a source-defined heuristic: an expensive elementwise operation contributes 16, an ordinary one contributes 1, and the default threshold is 16. The cast and multiply in this fold contribute 2; the add after the fold is not counted as per-element work. A fold containing exp reaches the threshold. These values classify a body for code generation; they are not measured cycle counts or speedups. LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:204 LegalizeRowwiseKernels.cpp:243 MOGGPasses.td:235

class MOGG_Op<string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
  Op<MOGGDialect, mnemonic, traits>;

// Ops that call a kernel, a primitive or a `mogg.func`.
def MOGG_CallLike : NativeOpTrait<"CallLike"> {
  let cppNamespace = "::M::MOGG";
}

class MOGG_LowerableOp<string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
  MOGG_Op<mnemonic, traits # [
    DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<LowerableToMGPInterface, ["lower"]>,
  ]>;

class MOGG_KernelTerminatorOp<string mnemonic, list<Trait> traits = []> :
  MOGG_Op<mnemonic, traits # [
    DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MOGG_KernelTerminator>,
    Terminator,
  ]>;

def DimensionType : ScalarOfDType<BoundAnd<DTypeConstraint<"*$_self == KGEN::KGENDType::si64">>, "!kgen.simd<1, si64>">,
    BuildableType<"KGEN::SIMDType::get(1, KGEN::DTypeConstantAttr::get("
                                   "$_builder.getContext(), KGEN::KGENDType::si64))">;

// Internal helper ops

def MOGG_ConcatOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"concat", [
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  MO_SingleDevice,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Concat Operation along axis zero";
  let description = [{
    Example:

    ```mlir
    %arg0: !mo.tensor<[3, 3], f32>
    %arg1: !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>
    %res = mogg.concat(%arg0, %arg1) : (
      !mo.tensor<[3, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>
    ) -> !mo.tensor<[5, 3], f32>
    ```

    Works for CUDA and host devices.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins Variadic<MO_Tensor>:$inputs);
  let results = (outs MO_Tensor:$result);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $inputs `)` attr-dict `:` functional-type($inputs, results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_SplitOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"split", [Pure]> {
  let summary = "Split Operation along axis zero";
  let description = [{
    `mo.split` with `axis` zero; the split sizes are implied by the result
    types.

    Example:

    ```mlir
    %input: !mo.tensor<[9, 8], f32>
    %res = mogg.split(%input) : (!mo.tensor<[9, 8], f32> ) ->
    (!mo.tensor<[2, 8], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3, 8], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4, 8], f32>)
    ```

    Currently only for the 'host' device.
    TODO: Generalize to arbitrary devices.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins MO_Tensor:$input);
  let results = (outs Variadic<MO_Tensor>:$results);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` `(`
      qualified(type($input)) `)` `->` `(` type($results) `)`
  }];
}

def MOGG_SliceOp : MOGG_Op<"slice", [
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  MO_SingleDeviceWithHostOperands<["start", "stop"]>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Contiguous zero-copy slice op lowerable to mgp.tensor.slice";
  let description = [{
    Unlike mo.slice, not lowered to a kernel by MOToMOGG. FuseViews lowers it
    to a mogg.routine temporarily and raises it back if unfused.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MO_Tensor:$input,
    MO_IndexScalarIfRanked:$start,
    MO_IndexScalarIfRanked:$stop
  );
  let results = (outs MO_Tensor:$result);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` attr-dict `:` functional-type(operands, results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_OutputOp : MOGG_Op<"output", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  ReturnLike,
  Terminator,
]> {
  let summary = "MOGG output operation";
  let description = [{
    Specifies the output values of a region in a MOGG operation.

    ```mlir
      mogg.op foo() {
      ... mogg.output e0, % 1 : i32, f8
    } : i32, f8
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins Variadic<AnyType>:$operands);
  let assemblyFormat = "attr-dict ($operands^ `:` type($operands))?";
}

def MOGG_CallOp : MOGG_Op<"call", [
  MOGG_CallLike,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
  MOGG_FuncCallOpInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Calls into an outlined stub";
  let description = [{}];
  let arguments = (ins
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$name,
    Variadic<AnyType>:$inputs,
    OptionalAttr<I64Attr>:$affinity_device_id
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$outputs);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $name ($inputs^ `:` type($inputs))? (`->` type($outputs)^)?
    (`affinity_device_id` `=` $affinity_device_id^)? attr-dict
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    FuncOp getCallee();
  }];
}

def MOGG_CallAsyncOp : MOGG_Op<"call.async", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
  MOGG_FuncCallOpInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Calls into an outlined stub asynchronously";
  let description = [{
    Dispatches via Mojo `create_task`. `affinity_device_id` pins the task to a
    CPU core with NUMA affinity for that GPU. It is a plain integer because
    kernel-layer device refs are label-only.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$name,
    Variadic<AnyType>:$inputs,
    OptionalAttr<I64Attr>:$affinity_device_id
  );
  let results = (outs MOGG_TaskHandle:$task_handle);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $name (`(` $inputs^ `:` type($inputs) `)`)?
    (`affinity_device_id` `=` $affinity_device_id^)? attr-dict
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    FuncOp getCallee();
  }];
}

def MOGG_CallBuildGraphOp : MOGG_Op<"call.build_graph", [
  AttrSizedOperandSegments,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MOGG_KernelCallInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<SymbolUserOpInterface>,
]> {
  let summary = "Record a kernel's `build_graph` function into a device-graph builder";
  let description = [{
    The device-graph counterpart of `mogg.call.execute`: invokes `build_graph`
    against a builder instead of `execute` against a context, recording a node
    rather than running the kernel. Produces no result; the enclosing
    `mgp.device_graph.dependencies` op orders nodes. Not a kernel terminator,
    and not wrapped in `mogg.with_trace`.

    `$hasEpilogueFusion` mirrors `mogg.call.opaque`: it is copied from the
    dispatch this call records and set the kernel's `has_epilogue_fusion`
    parameter, so a fused body reaches `build_graph` the same way it reaches
    `execute`.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    mogg.call.build_graph["linalg_kernels.__init__.Matmul"]
        inputs(%in, %wt : !mo.tensor<...>, !mo.tensor<...>)
        outputs(%out : !mo.tensor<...>)
        builder(%builder)

    // Lowered to
    Matmul.build_graph[...](out, in, wt, builder)
    ```
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    StrAttr:$kernelSymName,
    StrAttr:$moOpName,
    UnitAttr:$isThrows,
    Variadic<AnyTypeOf<[MOGG_Tensor, MOGG_Buffer, MOGG_Scalar, MOGG_Tuple,
                        MO_Opaque]>>:$inputs,
    Variadic<AnyTypeOf<[MOGG_Tensor, MOGG_Buffer, MOGG_Scalar, MOGG_Tuple,
                        MO_Opaque]>>:$outputs,
    MGP_DeviceGraphBuilderType:$graphBuilder,
    OptionalAttr<DictionaryAttr>:$kernel_param,
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$hasEpilogueFusion
  );

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `[` $kernelSymName `]` `` custom<OptionalKernelParams>($kernel_param)
    (`inputs` `(` $inputs^ `:` qualified(type($inputs)) `)`)?
    (`outputs` `(` $outputs^ `:` qualified(type($outputs)) `)`)?
    `builder` `(` $graphBuilder `)`
    (`isThrows` $isThrows^)?
    `moOpName` `=` $moOpName
    (`hasEpilogueFusion` `=` $hasEpilogueFusion^)?
    attr-dict
  }];
  let hasVerifier = 1;
}


def MOGG_AsyncRoutineOp : MOGG_Op<"routine.async", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_InOutSemanticsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MGP_LiftableChainCreateOpInterface>,
  DeclInterface,
  IsolatedFromAbove,
  MO_ExplicitDevice,
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
  SingleBlockImplicitTerminator<"MOGG::OutputOp">,
]> {
  let summary = "An abstract function representing a compiled body of code";
  let description = [{
    Takes and returns AsyncValues and runs its body to completion (always
    blocking). A generic form of mogg.routine; the first result is a mef.chain.

    Sequence fusion (concatenating code) fuses a parent region into a child:
    `canFuseIntoOther` allows this region as parent, `canBeFusedInto` as
    child. `canDuplicate` lets a region with several children be copied into
    each of them.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    Variadic<AnyType>:$operands,
    MO_ParamDecls:$outputParamDecls,
    M_InOutSignatureAttr:$inOutSignature,
    OptionalAttr<MOGG_FusionInfoAttr>:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    DefaultValuedAttr<ArrayAttr, "{}">:$constantResources,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canFuseIntoOther,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canBeFusedInto,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$canDuplicate,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$isStructured
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$results);
  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$body);
  let hasCanonicalizeMethod = 1;
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    custom<ImmediateDispatch>($dispatch)
    custom<Kernel>($operands, type($operands), type($results), $body,
                   $outputParamDecls)
    custom<FusionInfo>($fusionInfo)
    (`canBeFusedInto` `=` $canBeFusedInto^)?
    (`canDuplicate` `=` $canDuplicate^)?
    (`canFuseIntoOther` `=` $canFuseIntoOther^)?
    (`constantResources` `=` $constantResources^)?
    `inOutSignature` `=` $inOutSignature
    (`isStructured` `=` $isStructured^)?
    attr-dict
  }];

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    /// Required by DeclInterface.
    ArrayRef<ParamDeclAttr> getInputParams() { return {}; }

    Block &getBodyBlock() { return getBody().front(); }

    MOGG::OutputOp getBodyTerminator();
  }];
}

def MOGG_GetDimOp : MOGG_Op<"get_dim", [Pure]> {
  let summary = "Returns the runtime representation of a dimension";

  let arguments = (ins Builtin_StringAttr:$dimension);
  let results = (outs DimensionType:$result);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    custom<Dim>($dimension) attr-dict
  }];
}

def MOGG_ToMGPFromOpaqueOp : MOGG_Op<"to_mgp_from_opaque", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins AnyType:$input);
  let results = (outs AnyType:$dataPointer);
  let summary = "Get the opaque pointer from the kgen value";
  let description = [{
    A no-op that keeps IR types correct while converting a KGEN opaque value
    (e.g. mo.opaque for graph outputs) to !mgp.opaque. Folds away when the
    types match.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` operands `)` attr-dict `:`
        functional-type(operands, results)
  }];

  let hasFolder = 1;
}

def MOGG_ScratchPlaceholdersOp : MOGG_Op<"scratch_placeholders"> {
  let results = (outs Variadic<MO_Tensor>:$results);

  let summary = "Represents scratch buffer tensors that are not returned from the kernel";
  let description = [{
    Like `mogg.output_placeholders`, but the tensors are not returned from the
    kernel.

    Example:
    ```mlir
      %scratch = mogg.scratch_placeholders : !mo.tensor<[2, 3], f32>
    ```
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
   attr-dict `:` type($results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_CompiledLoadOp : MOGG_LowerableOp<"compiled.load"> {
  let summary = "Loads pairs of (symbol, compiled object) into the runtime "
                "for a given device.";
  let description = [{
    Registers each symbol with its compiled-object blob in the runtime, for
    use by ops like `CompiledCallOp`. The object format and registration
    depend on the op's device.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    ArrayAttr:$symbols,
    ConfinedAttr<
      ElementsAttr,
      [AnyAttrOf<[Builtin_DenseResourceElementsAttr]>]
    >:$value,
    DefaultValuedAttr<BoolAttr, "false">:$debuginfo
  );
}


def MOGG_CompiledCallOp : MOGG_Op<"compiled.call", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MemoryEffectsOpInterface>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<MO_ParamDeclaration>,
  MO_ExplicitDevice,
  MO_HasDeviceInterface,
]> {
  let summary = "Executes a compiled kernel on a given device.";
  let description = [{
    Looks up the compiled object (loaded by `CompiledLoadOp`) by name
    and calls it with the lowered operands.

    `usedParams` are the shape parameters the kernel uses; they are passed at
    runtime to reconstruct tensor shapes. `outputParamDecls` defines parameter
    values, which MGP translates into parameter system calls. `dispatch` says
    how the runtime schedules the call (see `MOGG_DispatchKind`).

    The kernel reads and writes memory its operands only point to, such as
    the buffer an init-block call fills, so the op is never pure: a call
    whose results are unused is not dead, and two identical calls are not
    redundant.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    Variadic<AnyType>:$operands,
    FlatSymbolRefAttr:$calleeSymbol,
    ArrayAttr:$usedParams,
    MO_ParamDecls:$outputParamDecls,
    OptionalAttr<MOGG_FusionInfoAttr>:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    ArrayAttr:$constantResources
  );
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$results);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $calleeSymbol `` custom<OutputParamDecls>($outputParamDecls)
    `` `(` $operands `)`
    custom<ImmediateDispatch>($dispatch)
    custom<FusionInfo>($fusionInfo)
    `constantResources` `=` $constantResources `,`
    `usedParams` `=` $usedParams
    attr-dict `:` functional-type($operands, $results)
  }];
}

def MOGG_FuncOp : MOGG_Op<"func", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  FunctionOpInterface,
  IsolatedFromAbove,
  SingleBlockImplicitTerminator<"MOGG::OutputOp">,
  SymbolName,
  SymbolVisibility,
  Symbol,
]> {
  let summary = "Op that outlines a kernel";
  let description = [{
    A kernel that will be compiled to Mojo text.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins
    SymbolNameAttr:$sym_name,
    TypeAttrOf<FunctionType>:$function_type,
    MOGG_FusionInfoAttr:$fusionInfo,
    DefaultValuedOptionalAttr<MOGG_DispatchKindAttr,
                              "::M::MOGG::DispatchKind::Immediate">:$dispatch,
    DefaultValuedAttr<ArrayAttr, "{}">:$constantResources,
    MOGG_ABIKindAttr:$abi,
    // Execution-device label for each kernel's `target` parameter. A string
    // rather than `#M.device_ref` because only the label matters.
    StrAttr:$device,
    OptionalAttr<ArrayAttr>:$trait_stub_buffer_capture,
    OptionalAttr<ArrayAttr>:$trait_stub_arg_bounds,
    // Needed by -symbol-dce.
    DefaultValuedAttr<StrAttr, "\"private\"">:$sym_visibility
  );

  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$body);

  let hasCustomAssemblyFormat = 1;
  let hasVerifier = 1;

  let extraClassDeclaration = [{
    Block &getBodyBlock() { return getBody().front(); }
    OutputOp getBodyTerminator();
    Region *getCallableRegion() { return &getBodyRegion(); }
    ArrayRef<Type> getArgumentTypes() {
      return getFunctionType().getInputs();
    }
    ArrayRef<Type> getResultTypes() {
      return getFunctionType().getResults();
    }

    mlir::ArrayAttr getArgAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    mlir::ArrayAttr getResAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    void setArgAttrsAttr(mlir::ArrayAttr attrs){}
    void setResAttrsAttr(mlir::ArrayAttr attrs){}
    mlir::Attribute removeArgAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }
    mlir::Attribute removeResAttrsAttr() { return nullptr; }

  private:
    mlir::LogicalResult emitMojoMGPABI(EmitMojoState &state);
    mlir::LogicalResult emitMojoMOGGABI(EmitMojoState &state);
  }];
}

def MOGG_TensorInitOp : MOGG_Op<"tensor.__init__", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Represents the construction of a tensor";
  let description = [{
    Lowers to a ManagedTensorSlice constructor call from a data pointer and
    dimensions.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    Variadic<SI64Scalar>:$dims,
    BoolAttr:$mut,
    MO_IOKind:$io
  );
  let results = (outs AnyTypeOf<[MO_Tensor, MO_Buffer]>:$tensor);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $buffer (`,` $dims^)? `)` `io` `=` custom<IOKind>($io) `,` `mut` `=` $mut
    attr-dict `:` qualified(type($buffer)) `->` qualified(type($tensor))
  }];
}

def MOGG_TensorArgInitOp : MOGG_Op<"tensor_arg.__init__", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  AttrSizedOperandSegments,
  Pure,
]> {
  let summary = "Construct a trait-lane tensor argument from its contract";
  let description = [{
    Like `mogg.tensor.__init__`, but carries the `#mogg.tensor_arg` contract
    for an argument satisfying a kernel trait bound, instead of `{io, mut}`.
    `role`/`access` are read from the contract, not the result type.

    `$device_context` is for the GPU emit path and is not yet populated.
    `contract.fused` is currently always false and `contract.access` `none`.
  }];

  let arguments = (ins
    MGP_DeviceBufferType:$buffer,
    Variadic<SI64Scalar>:$dims,
    Optional<MOGG_Context>:$device_context,
    MOGG_TensorArgContractAttr:$contract
  );
  let results = (outs AnyTypeOf<[MO_Tensor, MO_Buffer]>:$tensor);

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $buffer (`,` $dims^)? `)` (`context` `(` $device_context^ `)`)?
    `contract` `=` $contract
    attr-dict `:` qualified(type($buffer)) `->` qualified(type($tensor))
  }];
}

def MOGG_AsyncReadyOp : MOGG_Op<"async.ready", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  Pure,
]> {
  let results = (outs ChainType:$output);

  let summary = "Represents a chain output placeholder";
  let description = [{
    Resolves chain dependencies for data-dependent operations and lets fusion
    elide chains when lowering to a compiled region.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    attr-dict
  }];
}

def MOGG_AsyncJoinOp : MOGG_Op<"async.join", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins Variadic<MOGG_TaskHandle>:$task_handles);

  let summary = "Waits for async task handles and raises on error";
  let description = [{
    Waits for all tasks, then raises the first error, if any. Has no results;
    use `mogg.async.ready` for the output chain.

    Example:
    ```mlir
    mogg.async.join(%t0, %t1)
    ```
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $task_handles `)` attr-dict
  }];
}

def MOGG_AsyncUnpackOp : MOGG_Op<"async.unpack", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
  InferTypeOpAdaptor,
  Pure,
  TypesMatchWith<"input is the async wrapper of the result",
                 /*lhs=*/"output", /*rhs=*/"input",
                 "::M::MOGG::AsyncType::get($_self)">,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_Async:$input);
  let results = (outs AnyType:$output);
  let summary = "Unpacks an async value and returns it as sync";
  let description = [{
    Projects `!mogg.async<T>` (values outside a `mogg.routine.async`)
    to `T`. Inverse of `mogg.async.pack`. Only `T` is printed.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` type($output)
  }];

  let hasFolder = 1;
}

def MOGG_AsyncPackOp : MOGG_Op<"async.pack", [

  }];

    `(` $input `)` attr-dict `:` type($input)
  }];

  let hasFolder = 1;
}

def MOGG_YieldOp : MOGG_Op<"yield", [

]> {

  let description = [{
    Yields the results of a mogg.try / except, the value a
    `mogg.tensor.create.prologue` body returns to the reading kernel, the
    value a compute `mogg.tensor.create.epilogue` body returns for the kernel
    to store, or an element's contribution to a `mogg.rowwise.reduce`.

def MOGG_WithTraceOp : MOGG_Op<"with_trace", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Wraps a kernel terminator in a Trace context manager";
  let description = [{
    Models `with Trace[...]` around the KernelTerminator of a MOGG ABI stub.
    Always throwing because Trace.__enter__ raises.
  }];
  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$outputs);
  let regions = (region SizedRegion<1>:$body);

def MOGG_ProfileScopeBeginOp : MOGG_Op<"profile_scope.begin", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Opens a trace range for a Graph.profile_scope() span";
  let description = [{
    Lowers to `var t = Trace[...](name, color=...); t.start()`.

    A region-less sibling of `mogg.with_trace`: values defined inside a region
    would be invisible to later ops, and sequence-fused bodies have SSA values
    live across scope boundaries.

    `color` is set only when every covered op agrees on one (see
    `resolveProfileScopeColor`). Always throwing because `Trace.start()`
    raises.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins StrAttr:$name, OptionalAttr<StrAttr>:$color);
  let results = (outs MOGG_ProfileScopeRange:$range);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $name (`color` `=` $color^)? attr-dict
  }];
}

def MOGG_ProfileScopeEndOp : MOGG_Op<"profile_scope.end", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Closes the trace range opened by a `mogg.profile_scope.begin`";
  let description = [{
    Lowers to `t.end()`. Always throwing because `Trace.end()` raises.
  }];
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_ProfileScopeRange:$range);
  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $range attr-dict
  }];
}

def MOGG_TryOp : MOGG_Op<"try", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface, ["isThrows"]>,
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<OpAsmOpInterface, ["getAsmBlockArgumentNames"]>,
]> {
  let summary = "Op that represent a try / except statement";

    The except region takes the raised `!mogg.error` as its only argument,
    printed as `except(%err)`.
  }];

  let results = (outs Variadic<AnyType>:$outputs);

    attr-dict `:` type($outputs)

def MOGG_AsyncErrorOp : MOGG_Op<"async.error", [
  DeclareOpInterfaceMethods<EmitsMojoInterface>,
]> {
  let arguments = (ins MOGG_Error:$error);
  let results = (outs AnyType:$output);

  let summary = "Represents setting an error on a kernel output";
  let description = [{
    Sets an error on a chain or non-tensor output in a raising kernel's except
    block.

    ```
    mogg.try {
     ...
    } except(%err) {
      %chain = mogg.async.error %err : !mef.chain
      %dim0 = mogg.async.error %err : !si64
      mogg.yield %chain, %dim0
    }
    ```

    Lowers to `mogg_async_error_value`, returning an error `AnyAsyncValueRef`.
  }];

  let assemblyFormat = [{
    $error attr-dict `:` type(results)
  }];
}
