# Mixed-lane e2e proof: a trait-bound dense output alongside two legacy
# `InputTensor` operands in the same `execute` signature, computing
# `z[i] = x[i] + y[i]`. Confirms the trait-lane and legacy-lane capture
# assembly compose in the same `CallExecuteOp::emitMojo` call.
@extensibility.register("trait_mixed_legacy_add")
struct TraitMixedLegacyAdd:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & TileTensorable],
        x: InputTensor,
        y: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), TileTensorable)
        var zt = z.to_tile_tensor()
        var n = x.size()
        var zf = zt.reshape(row_major(n))
        for i in range(n):
            var xv = x[i]
            var yv = rebind[Scalar[type_of(x).dtype]](y[i])
            zf.store((i,), rebind[SIMD[type_of(zt).dtype, 1]](xv + yv))


# Mirror of `trait_mixed_legacy_add` with the lanes swapped: a legacy
# `OutputTensor` alongside two trait-bound dense inputs, so the legacy write
# path (`OutputTensor.__setitem__`) and the trait read path
# (`.to_tile_tensor().load`) both fire in the same emitted kernel.
@extensibility.register("trait_mixed_legacy_out_add")
struct TraitMixedLegacyOutAdd:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: OutputTensor,
        x: Some[Input & TileTensorable],
        y: Some[Input & TileTensorable],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(y), TileTensorable)
        var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
        var yt = y.to_tile_tensor[type_of(x).dtype]()
        var n = Int(x.shape().product())
        var xf = xt.reshape(row_major(n))
        var yf = yt.reshape(row_major(n))
        for i in range(n):
            var xv = xf.load[width=1]((i,))
            var yv = yf.load[width=1]((i,))
            z[i] = rebind[Scalar[z.dtype]](xv + yv)


# One-value-two-lanes proof: a trait-bound dense input NEXT TO a legacy
# `InputTensor` input, computing `z[i] = x[i] + y[i]`. Called with the same
# graph value on both input positions, `SimplifyKernelOperands` merges the
# duplicates into one exec-body argument that must then materialize one
# representation per lane (the GEX-4071 per-use init split) — one
# `mogg.tensor_arg.__init__` for the trait position and one
# `mogg.tensor.__init__` for the legacy position, over the same buffer.
@extensibility.register("trait_dual_lane_add")
struct TraitDualLaneAdd:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: OutputTensor,
        x: Some[Input & TileTensorable],
        y: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
        var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
        var n = y.size()
        var xf = xt.reshape(row_major(n))
        for i in range(n):
            var xv = xf.load[width=1]((i,))
            var yv = rebind[SIMD[type_of(xt).dtype, 1]](y[i])
            z[i] = rebind[Scalar[z.dtype]](xv + yv)

# 3 inputs / 1 output: `res = a + b + c`.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_add3")
struct MapLowerAdd3:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        c: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            return (
                rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx))
                + rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](b.load[width](idx))
                + rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](c.load[width](idx))
            )

        foreach[target=target](func, res, ctx)


# 1 input / 2 outputs: `res0 = a + 1`, `res1 = a * 2` (two plain outputs, two
# independent `foreach` loops).
@extensibility.register("map_lower_two_outputs")
struct MapLowerTwoOutputs:

        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res0: OutputTensor,
        res1: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:

        def add_one[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res0.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res0.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) + 1

        foreach(add_one, res0, ctx)

        @inline(.always)
        def times_two[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res1.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res1.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) * 2

        foreach(times_two, res1, ctx)


# 2 inputs / 2 outputs: `res0 = a + b`, `res1 = a - b`.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_add_sub")
struct MapLowerAddSub:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res0: OutputTensor,
        res1: OutputTensor,
        a: InputTensor,
        b: InputTensor,
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def add[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res0.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res0.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) + rebind[
                SIMD[res0.dtype, width]
            ](b.load[width](idx))

        foreach[target=target](add, res0, ctx)

        @inline(.always)
        def sub[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res1.dtype, width]:
            return rebind[SIMD[res1.dtype, width]](a.load[width](idx)) - rebind[
                SIMD[res1.dtype, width]
            ](b.load[width](idx))

        foreach[target=target](sub, res1, ctx)

# Variadic operand: `res = sum(inputs)` over an `InputVariadicTensors`.
# Exercises the MAP `tuple.create` materialization path. Modeled on the
# signature-only `map_lower_variadic` but with a real summing body.
@extensibility.register("map_lower_var_sum")
struct MapLowerVarSum:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        size: Int,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        res: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=1, ...],
        inputs: InputVariadicTensors[dtype=dtype, rank=1, size=size, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        @inline(.always)
        def func[width: Int](idx: Coord) {var} -> SIMD[res.dtype, width]:
            var acc = SIMD[res.dtype, width](0)

            comptime for i in range(size):
                acc += rebind[SIMD[res.dtype, width]](
                    inputs[i].load[width](idx)
                )

            return acc

        foreach(func, res, ctx)

# `trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat` through a host-built unified closure: the
# host projects the whole tuple to its access-enabled views with
# `TensorTuple._fused_view(inputs)`, the device closure copy-captures the view
# tuple, and the body loads element `k` through it. The view tuple is
# `RegisterPassable` only conditionally, which the closure emitter proves from
# the tuple's bindings. GPU only.
@extensibility.register("trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat_unified_closure")
struct TraitTensorTupleFusedConcatUnifiedClosure:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        Ins: TypeList[Trait=Input & Fused & LoadAccess, ...],
        //,
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & TileTensorable],
        inputs: TensorTuple[*Ins],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            raise Error(
                "trait_tensor_tuple_fused_concat_unified_closure only runs on"
                " the GPU"
            )
        else:
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), TileTensorable)
            var zt = z.to_tile_tensor()
            comptime out_dtype = type_of(zt).dtype
            var offsets = StaticTuple[Int32, len(Ins) + 1](fill=0)
            comptime for k in range(len(Ins)):
                offsets[k + 1] = offsets[k] + Int32(
                    Int(inputs[k].shape().product())
                )
            var n_dev = offsets[len(Ins)]
            var views = TensorTuple._fused_view(inputs)

            def device_body() {var views, var zt, var offsets, var n_dev}:
                var i = Int32(global_idx.x)
                if i >= n_dev:
                    return
                comptime for k in range(len(Ins)):
                    if i >= offsets[k] and i < offsets[k + 1]:
                        comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(views[k]), Loadable)
                        zt.reshape(row_major(Int(n_dev))).store(
                            (Int(i),),
                            views[k]
                            .load[1]((Int(i - offsets[k]),))
                            .cast[out_dtype](),
                        )

            comptime block_size = 64
            ctx.enqueue_function(
                device_body,
                grid_dim=(ceildiv(Int(n_dev), block_size),),
                block_dim=(block_size,),
            )


# A kernel with two `execute` overloads under one registration
# (`supports_unfused_execute`). The graph compiler calls the fused one when
# any output has a fused epilogue, with an identity epilogue on the others, and
# the plain one when none has, so the kernel keeps a direct store path without
# branching on `has_epilogue_fusion`. The plain overload needs its `where`
# clause: a fused output wrapper is a `Tensor` too, and Mojo does not rank the
# fused overload's bound as more specific. `z` is `x + 1` through either
# overload; `w` records which ran: 1 fused, 0 plain.
@extensibility.register("trait_unfused_execute")
struct TraitUnfusedExecute:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & Fused & StoreAccess],
        w: Some[Output & Fused & StoreAccess],
        x: Some[Input & Tensor],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert (
            type_of(x).rank == 1
            and type_of(z).rank == 1
            and type_of(w).rank == 1
        )
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), Storable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(w), Storable)
            var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
            for i in range(Int(xt.dim[0]())):
                var raw = rebind[SIMD[type_of(z).dtype, 1]](xt.load((i,))) + 1
                z.store[1](Coord(i), raw)
                w.store[1](Coord(i), SIMD[type_of(w).dtype, 1](1))
        else:
            raise Error("trait_unfused_execute is CPU-only")

    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        target: StaticString,
    ](
        z: Some[Output & Tensor],
        w: Some[Output & Tensor],
        x: Some[Input & Tensor],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises where not conforms_to(type_of(z), Fused):
        comptime assert (
            type_of(x).rank == 1
            and type_of(z).rank == 1
            and type_of(w).rank == 1
        )
        comptime if is_cpu[target]():
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(x), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(z), TileTensorable)
            comptime assert conforms_to(type_of(w), TileTensorable)
            var xt = x.to_tile_tensor()
            var zt = z.to_tile_tensor()
            var wt = w.to_tile_tensor()
            for i in range(Int(xt.dim[0]())):
                var raw = rebind[SIMD[type_of(zt).dtype, 1]](xt.load((i,))) + 1
                zt.store((i,), raw)
                wt.store((i,), SIMD[type_of(wt).dtype, 1](0))
        else:
            raise Error("trait_unfused_execute is CPU-only")

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// A `map.constant` has no operand to arrive on, so it lowers to a
// `mogg.buffer.constant` -- a pointer straight from the bytes -- and its tensor
// is rebuilt from that pointer exactly like an input's. Note the kernel takes
// no input pointer at all here: the constant is not an operand.
//
// The bytes stay unaligned. `MOGGToMGP` turns this into an
// `mgp.buffer.constant` at the call site, where the pipeline's minimum CPU
// alignment is known.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @constant
// CHECK: mogg.routine () -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
// CHECK-NEXT: outputs ([[OP:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT: context ([[CTX:%[^ :,]+]])
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[OSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create()
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[OT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[OP]], [[OSH]]) {{.*}}io = Output, mut = true
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[CP:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.buffer.constant #M.dense_array<1.000000e+00, 2.000000e+00, 3.000000e+00, 4.000000e+00> : tensor<2x2xf32>
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[CSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create()
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[CT:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.create([[CP]], [[CSH]]) {{.*}}io = Input, mut = false
// CHECK-NEXT:   [[LSH:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.shape.create()
// CHECK-NEXT:   mogg.call.foreach {{.*}} ([[IDX:%[^ :,]+]] : !map.index<2>) capturing {[[CIN:%[^ :,]+]] = [[CT]] : !mogg.tensor, [[OUT:%[^ :,]+]] = [[OT]] : !mogg.tensor}
// CHECK-NEXT:     [[CV:%[^ ]+]] = mogg.tensor.load [[CIN]][[[IDX]]]
// CHECK-NEXT:     mogg.tensor.store [[OUT]][[[IDX]]] = [[CV]]
mo.graph @constant() -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %r = map.iter.opaque
      inputs ()
      outputs (%out : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) {
    %c = map.constant #M.dense_array<1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0> : tensor<2x2xf32> : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
    map.iter.elementwise.body<[2, 2]>
        index (%idx: !map.index<2>)
        capturing {%c0 = %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, %out0 = %out : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>} {
      %cv = map.load %c0[%idx] : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
      map.store %out0[%idx] = %cv : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
    }
  } {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>}
  mo.output %r : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-pipeline --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s
//
// And, after `ConformCallOperands`, the read-only operand is recreated immutable
// (this is the fix; without it the call would carry a mutable slice the kernel's
// immutable parameter rejects at codegen).
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-pipeline --map-to-mogg --mogg-conform-call-operands | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=CONFORM

// `FuseMutableLoads` fuses a `mo.mutable.load` into an opaque kernel operand the
// kernel only reads -- here `map_lower_inplace_copy`'s immutable `src`. MAPToMOGG
// reconstructs every buffer operand as a mutable `mogg.tensor.create`
// (a `!mogg.buffer`), so both `dst` and the fused-read `src` come out mutable.
// `ConformCallOperands` then reconciles the read-only `src`: it accepts the
// mut->immut widening (OperandInference) and clones that operand's
// `mogg.tensor.create` immutable (`cloneWithMut`), yielding a `!mogg.tensor`
// whose codegen slice matches the kernel's `Input` parameter. `dst`, which the
// kernel genuinely writes, stays a mutable `!mogg.buffer`.

// Before conform: MAPToMOGG makes both operands mutable buffers.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}}: !mogg.buffer
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}}: !mogg.buffer
// CHECK:     mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : !mogg.buffer, !mogg.buffer)

// After conform: the read-only src is recreated immutable and the call uses it.
// CONFORM-LABEL: mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input
// CONFORM:     mogg.tensor.create({{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = false{{.*}}: !mogg.tensor
// CONFORM:     mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerInplaceCopy inputs(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}} : !mogg.buffer, !mogg.tensor)
mo.graph @fused_mutable_load_into_immutable_input(%dst: !mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, %srcbuf: !mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.chain {
  %chain = mo.chain.create()
  %src, %loadchain = mo.mutable.load(%srcbuf, %chain) : (!mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain)
  %outchain = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_inplace_copy", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%dst, %src, %chain) : (!mo.buffer<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.chain) -> !mo.chain
  mo.output %outchain : !mo.chain
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/Conversion/MAPToMOGG/shape-func-kgen-params.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// mo.invoke_shape_func has no MAP form, so map-to-mogg lowers it directly. Its
// `kgenParams` are ordinary parameters of the shape function and must reach the
// call alongside the declared `output_rank`; forwarding only the rank leaves
// `axis` uninferable at emit time.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @gatherShapeFuncKgenParams
// CHECK: mogg.call.shape @{{.*}}gather_shape_fn
// CHECK-SAME: [axis = -2 : index, output_rank = 4 : index]
mo.graph @gatherShapeFuncKgenParams<() -> D0, D1, D2, D3>(
    %input: !mo.tensor<[1, 2, 3], f32>,
    %indices: !mo.tensor<[4, 5], f32>
) -> !mo.tensor<[D0, D1, D2, D3], si32> {
  mo.invoke_shape_func["mo.gather"]<() -> D4, D5, D6, D7>(%input, %indices)
    [kgenParams = {axis = -2 : index}, dataDeptTensors = []] :
    (!mo.tensor<[1, 2, 3], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4, 5], f32>)

  %one = mo.constant <#M.dense_array<1> : tensor<si32>> : !mo.tensor<[], si32>
  %val = mo.static.broadcast_to(%one): !mo.tensor<[], si32> -> !mo.tensor<[D4, D5, D6, D7], si32>

  mo.output<D4, D5, D6, D7> %val : !mo.tensor<[D4, D5, D6, D7], si32>
}

// reduce-shaped.
func.func @storeOutsideEmit(%shape: !mogg.shape, %ctx: !mogg.context, %x: !mogg.tensor, %out: !mogg.tensor, %copy: !mogg.tensor) {
  // expected-error @below{{stores outside its emit; only reduce-shaped bodies are supported}}
  mogg.call.rowwise shape(%shape) axis(1) context(%ctx) (%row : !map.index<2>) capturing {%cx = %x : !mogg.tensor, %co = %out : !mogg.tensor, %cc = %copy : !mogg.tensor} device = "cpu" {
    %acc = mogg.rowwise.reduce @builtin_kernels.monoids.ReduceSum (%i : !map.index<2>) -> !mogg.simd<f32> {
      %v = mogg.tensor.load %cx[%i] : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2> -> !mogg.simd<f32>
      mogg.tensor.store %cc[%i] = %v : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2>, !mogg.simd<f32>
      mogg.yield %v : !mogg.simd<f32>
    }
    mogg.tensor.store %co[%row] = %acc : !mogg.tensor, !map.index<2>, !mogg.simd<f32>
  }
  return
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/MOGGDialect/Transforms/LegalizeRowwiseKernels/legalize.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies --map-to-mogg --mogg-legalize-rowwise-kernels | FileCheck %s

// A fused reduction, from MO to a rowwise kernel ready to print as Mojo.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @sumOfSquaresPlusBias
// CHECK:       mogg.call.rowwise {{.*}} attributes {accum = f32, cols = 128 : i64, dtype = bf16, dtype_size = 0 : i64, num_phases = 1 : i64, primary = 0 : i64, simd_monoid = @builtin_kernels.monoids.ReduceSum} {
// CHECK-NEXT:    %[[ACC:.*]] = mogg.rowwise.reduce @builtin_kernels.monoids.ReduceSum (%i : !map.index<2>) -> !mogg.simd<f32> {
// CHECK-NEXT:      %[[P:.*]] = mogg.rowwise.primary : !mogg.simd<bf16>
// CHECK-NEXT:      %[[A:.*]] = mogg.call.elementwise @builtin_kernels.elementwise.Cast(%[[P]])
// CHECK-NEXT:      %[[SQ:.*]] = mogg.call.elementwise @builtin_kernels.elementwise.Mul(%[[A]], %[[A]])
// CHECK-NEXT:      mogg.yield %[[SQ]] : !mogg.simd<f32>
// CHECK-NEXT:    } {fields = ["acc"], params = {dtype = f32}}
// CHECK-NEXT:    %[[B:.*]] = mogg.tensor.load %cap1[%row]
// CHECK-NEXT:    %[[Y:.*]] = mogg.call.elementwise @builtin_kernels.elementwise.Add(%[[ACC]], %[[B]])
// CHECK-NEXT:    mogg.rowwise.emit {
// CHECK-NEXT:      mogg.tensor.store %cap2[%row] = %[[Y]]
// CHECK-NEXT:    }
// CHECK-NEXT:  }
mo.graph @sumOfSquaresPlusBias(%x: !mo.tensor<[8, 128], bf16>, %b: !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32> {
  %a = mo.cast(%x) : (!mo.tensor<[8, 128], bf16>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>
  %sq = mo.mul(%a, %a) : !mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>
  %r = mo.reduce.add(%sq) : (!mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>
  %y = mo.add(%r, %b) : !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>
  mo.output %y : !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>
}

// An exp in the fold makes the kernel computationally expensive.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @sumOfExp
// CHECK:       mogg.call.rowwise {{.*}} computationally_expensive,
// CHECK:         mogg.call.elementwise @builtin_kernels.elementwise.Exp
mo.graph @sumOfExp(%x: !mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32> {
  %e = mo.exp(%x) : !mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>
  %r = mo.reduce.add(%e) : (!mo.tensor<[8, 128], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>
  mo.output %r : !mo.tensor<[8, 1], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/MOGGDialect/Transforms/codegen-map-abi-stub.mlir · complete source
// RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
// RUN: env MODULAR_DEBUG=ir-output-dir=%t mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg --mogg-conform-call-operands \
// RUN:   --mogg-outline-routines --mogg-emit-mojo -verify-each=false
// RUN: FileCheck %s < %t/graph.mojo

// End-to-end Mojo emission for the MOGG-ABI `mogg.func`
// (FuncOp::emitMojoMOGGABI plus the shape.create / tensor.create /
// call.opaque / scalar.create / tuple.create emitters). The MOGG stub takes raw
// `!mogg.pointer` / `!mogg.dim` / `!mogg.context` handles and reconstructs the
// codegen tensors internally before invoking the opaque kernel's execute
// function.
//
// The pipeline is stopped right after emission: the surrounding `mogg.routine`
// container is only consumed later (MOGGToMGP + region outlining), so its
// `mogg.call` dangles once emit erases the stub -- `-verify-each=false`
// tolerates that. The emitted Mojo is read from the `ir-output-dir` dump rather
// than `--mogg-dump-mojo`, which needs a fully lowered `mgp.model`.

// Plain output: static shape -> compile-time `Idx[N]` Coord, a raw-pointer
// `mogg_tensor_init` per tensor, and a DPS execute call (output, input, ctx).
// CHECK: def {{__[A-Za-z0-9_]+}}({{.*}}: OpaquePointer[MutAnyOrigin], {{.*}}: OpaquePointer[MutAnyOrigin], [[PC:.*]]: {{.*}}DeviceContext) raises:
// CHECK:   var [[PSHAPE:.*]] = layout.Coord(layout.Idx[2], layout.Idx[2])
// CHECK:   var [[PLAYOUT:.*]] = layout.row_major([[PSHAPE]])
// CHECK:   var [[PIN:.*]] = {{.*}}mogg_tensor_init[DType.float32, 2, False, extensibility.IO.Input, {{[0-9]+}}]({{.*}}.unsafe_bitcast[NoneType](), [[PLAYOUT]])
// CHECK:   var [[POUT:.*]] = {{.*}}mogg_tensor_init[DType.float32, 2, True, extensibility.IO.Output, {{[0-9]+}}]({{.*}}.unsafe_bitcast[NoneType](), {{.*}})
// CHECK:   {{.*}}.MapLowerOnePlainOutput.execute[target = "cpu"]([[POUT]], [[PIN]], [[PC]])

mo.graph @plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Dynamic dim: the `!mogg.dim` handle arrives as a trailing `Int` argument and
// feeds a runtime `Scalar[DType.int]` Coord component.
// CHECK: def {{__[A-Za-z0-9_]+}}({{.*}}: OpaquePointer[MutAnyOrigin], {{.*}}: OpaquePointer[MutAnyOrigin], [[DIM:.*]]: Int, {{.*}}: {{.*}}DeviceContext) raises:
// CHECK:   var {{.*}} = layout.Coord(Scalar[DType.int]([[DIM]]), layout.Idx[4])

mo.graph @dyn(%a: !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
}

// Scalar operand: `scalar.create` packs the single-element tensor into a scalar
// via `mogg_as_scalar`, passed after the input in the DPS execute call.
// CHECK: def {{__[A-Za-z0-9_]+}}(
// CHECK:   var [[SC:.*]] = {{.*}}mogg_as_scalar({{.*}})
// CHECK:   {{.*}}.MapLowerScalar.execute[target = "cpu"]({{.*}}, {{.*}}, [[SC]], {{.*}})

mo.graph @scalar(%a: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>, %s: !mo.tensor<[], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32> {

// A throwing shape function gets both wrappers and still returns: each
// forwards the shape out, so it survives both hops. Without that forwarding
// the shape is computed inside a region and discarded.

// CHECK:       def __shapeof_imposter_add_raising_shape{{[_0-9]*}}(
// CHECK-SAME:    -> std.utils.IndexList[
// CHECK:         var [[OUT:[a-z_0-9]+]]: std.utils.IndexList[
// CHECK:         try:
// CHECK:           var [[TRACED:[a-z_0-9]+]]: std.utils.IndexList[

// CHECK:             var [[VAL:[a-z_0-9]+]] = {{.*}}imposter_add_raising_shape_shape(
// CHECK:             [[TRACED]] = [[VAL]]
// CHECK:           [[OUT]] = [[TRACED]]
// CHECK:         except
// CHECK:           raise
// CHECK:         return [[OUT]]

mo.graph @raising_shape<D0 -> D1>(%a: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>, %b: !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D1], f32> {
  %r = mo.custom<() -> D2> [symbol = "imposter_add_raising_shape", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a, %b) : (!mo.tensor<[D0], f32>, !mo.tensor<[D0], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[D2], f32>

}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=DECL
// RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
// RUN: env MODULAR_DEBUG=ir-output-dir=%t mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers \
// RUN:   --map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies \
// RUN:   --canonicalize --cse --map-to-mogg \
// RUN:   --mogg-conform-call-operands \
// RUN:   --mogg-outline-routines --mogg-to-mgp --mogg-emit-mojo \
// RUN:   -verify-each=false
// RUN: cat %t/*.mojo | FileCheck %s

// `trait_unfused_execute` registers a fused and an unfused `execute`. Import
// records the fused signature plus the flag.
// DECL: mogg.kernel.decl @testing_kernels.testing_kernels.TraitUnfusedExecute registration = "trait_unfused_execute"
// DECL-SAME: supports_unfused_execute

// Mojo emission, one function per graph in graph order. With nothing fused,
// `ConformCallOperands` drops the pass-through epilogues and hands the kernel
// its outputs as plain dense arguments, so Mojo resolves the plain overload.
// CHECK-LABEL: def __custom__trait_unfused_execute{{[_0-9a-f]*}}(
// CHECK-NOT:   _MoggOutputStoreFusionTensor
// CHECK:       _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{[^,]+}}, {{[^,]+}}, {{[0-9]+}}, _MoggTensorIO.OUTPUT
// CHECK:       _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{[^,]+}}, {{[^,]+}}, {{[0-9]+}}, _MoggTensorIO.OUTPUT
// CHECK:       TraitUnfusedExecute.execute[target = "cpu"]
mo.graph @unfused(%x: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) {
  %z, %w = mo.custom [symbol = "trait_unfused_execute", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%x) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>)
  mo.output %z, %w : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}

// Fusing into `w` keeps the fused form for both outputs: `z` gets its
// pass-through store functor.
// CHECK-LABEL: def __custom__trait_unfused_execute{{[_0-9a-f]*}}(
// CHECK:       _MoggOutputStoreFusionTensor[
// CHECK:       _MoggOutputStoreFusionTensor[
// CHECK:       TraitUnfusedExecute.execute[target = "cpu"]
mo.graph @fused_other(%x: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) {
  %z, %w = mo.custom [symbol = "trait_unfused_execute", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%x) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>)
  %w2 = mo.add(%w, %x) : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  mo.output %z, %w2 : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg | FileCheck %s

// A fused trait argument cannot be wrapped by `mogg.trait.create` downstream:
// its fusion functor is a local of the prologue/epilogue emit. So the contract
// is stamped onto the `mogg.tensor.create.prologue` / `.epilogue` producer at
// MAP lowering (where the fused-tensor -> call edge is still explicit), and emit
// reads that attr to wrap the functor in the conforming trait tensor rather than
// binding it onto a `ManagedTensorSlice`. Here we only assert the stamp on the
// prologue (the fused-input lane); the wrap + numerics, and the epilogue lane
// (which needs the accumulating-buffer pass), are covered by the e2e tests.

// `trait_fused_load_negate` declares its input `Some[Input & Fused & LoadAccess]`,
// so the `mo.add` producer fuses into it and the prologue carries a `load` input
// contract.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @fused_load
// CHECK: mogg.tensor.create.prologue
// CHECK-SAME: contract = <{role = input, fused = true, access = load
mo.graph @fused_load(%x: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32> {
  %p = mo.add(%x, %x) : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  %z = mo.custom [symbol = "trait_fused_load_negate", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%p) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  mo.output %z : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}
GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/MOGGDialect/Transforms/conform-trait-args.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg --mogg-conform-call-operands | FileCheck %s

// ConformCallOperands wraps each trait-bound call operand in a
// `mogg.trait.create` carrying the distilled contract, so a raw
// `!mogg.tensor` (which reconstructs as a `ManagedTensorSlice`, conforming to
// neither `Tensor` nor `TileTensorable`) reaches the kernel as the
// conforming trait argument. The wrap is materialized in the IR here; the call
// op's own emit stays a dumb forward. `trait_negate` declares both its input
// and its output against `TileTensorable`, so both operands are wrapped --
// with the input carrying `role = input` and the output `role = output` -- and the
// execution device rides on the op for local alignment at emit.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @trait_negate_graph
// CHECK: %[[INTENSOR:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = false{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[OUTTENSOR:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[INARG:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%[[INTENSOR]]) contract = <{role = input, fused = false, access = none, capabilities = none}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[OUTARG:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%[[OUTTENSOR]]) contract = <{role = output, fused = false, access = none, capabilities = none}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}TraitNegate inputs(%[[INARG]] : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%[[OUTARG]] : !mogg.tensor) context(
mo.graph @trait_negate_graph(%x: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32> {
  %z = mo.custom [symbol = "trait_negate", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%x) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  mo.output %z : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}

// RUN: MAX_GC_USE_ADV_FUSION=1 mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-to-mogg --mogg-conform-call-operands | FileCheck %s

// RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
// RUN: env MODULAR_DEBUG=ir-output-dir=%t MAX_GC_USE_ADV_FUSION=1 mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers \
// RUN:   --map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies \
// RUN:   --canonicalize --cse --map-to-mogg \
// RUN:   --mogg-conform-call-operands \
// RUN:   --mogg-outline-routines --mogg-to-mgp --mogg-emit-mojo \
// RUN:   -verify-each=false -o /dev/null
// RUN: cat %t/*.mojo | FileCheck %s --check-prefix=MOJO

// `trait_tensor_tuple_add` takes `outputs: TensorTuple[*Outs]`, `bias`, and
// `inputs: TensorTuple[*Ins]`. ConformCallOperands wraps every tuple element in
// its own `mogg.trait.create`, as it would a single trait argument, then packs
// each run into a `mogg.tuple.create` with the `tensor_tuple` ABI.

// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @trait_tensor_tuple_add_graph
// CHECK: %[[BIAS:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%{{.*}}) contract = <{role = input, {{.*}}}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[IN0:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%{{.*}}) contract = <{role = input, {{.*}}}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[IN1:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%{{.*}}) contract = <{role = input, {{.*}}}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[INS:.*]] = mogg.tuple.create(%[[IN0]], %[[IN1]]) variadic_abi = <tensor_tuple> : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[OUT0:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%{{.*}}) contract = <{role = output, {{.*}}}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[OUT1:.*]] = mogg.trait.create(%{{.*}}) contract = <{role = output, {{.*}}}>, device = {{.*}} : (!mogg.tensor) -> !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: %[[OUTS:.*]] = mogg.tuple.create(%[[OUT0]], %[[OUT1]]) variadic_abi = <tensor_tuple> : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}TraitTensorTupleAdd inputs(%[[BIAS]], %[[INS]] : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tuple) outputs(%[[OUTS]] : !mogg.tuple)

// Emit builds a `TensorTuple` holding each run's trait arguments and passes
// the tuples positionally. The `TypeList` parameters are infer-only, so the
// call leaves them to Mojo.
// MOJO: var [[BIAS:[a-z0-9_]+]] = _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{.*}}_MoggTensorIO.INPUT
// MOJO: var [[IN0:[a-z0-9_]+]] = _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{.*}}_MoggTensorIO.INPUT
// MOJO: var [[IN1:[a-z0-9_]+]] = _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{.*}}_MoggTensorIO.INPUT
// MOJO: var [[INS:[a-z0-9_]+]] = extensibility.TensorTuple[type_of([[IN0]]), type_of([[IN1]])]([[IN0]], [[IN1]])
// MOJO: var [[OUT0:[a-z0-9_]+]] = _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{.*}}_MoggTensorIO.OUTPUT
// MOJO: var [[OUT1:[a-z0-9_]+]] = _MoggDenseTensorArg[{{.*}}_MoggTensorIO.OUTPUT
// MOJO: var [[OUTS:[a-z0-9_]+]] = extensibility.TensorTuple[type_of([[OUT0]]), type_of([[OUT1]])]([[OUT0]], [[OUT1]])
// MOJO: TraitTensorTupleAdd.execute[target = "cpu"]([[OUTS]], [[BIAS]], [[INS]], {{[a-z0-9_]+}})
mo.graph @trait_tensor_tuple_add_graph(%bias: !mo.tensor<[1], f32>, %a: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>, %b: !mo.tensor<[3], f64>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>) {
  %z0, %z1 = mo.custom [symbol = "trait_tensor_tuple_add", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>] (%bias, %a, %b) : (
    !mo.tensor<[1], f32>,
    !mo.tensor<[2], si32>,
    !mo.tensor<[3], f64>
  ) -> (!mo.tensor<[2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>)
  mo.output %z0, %z1 : !mo.tensor<[2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>
}

// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mo-to-map --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers --map-to-mogg --mogg-outline-routines | FileCheck %s

// OutlineRoutines moves each `mogg.routine` body into a module-level
// `mogg.func` labeled with the MOGG ABI, and replaces the kernel body
// with a single `mogg.call` forwarding the pointer / dim / context block
// args. The `mogg.routine` container is kept for `MOGGToMGP`.
//
// The stub is named `__<ops it fuses>`; two kernels that fuse the same ops share
// a preferred name, so the symbol table appends a numeric suffix to the second
// (`..._0`), as `@dyn` and `@one_plain` show below.

// Plain output: the kernel body becomes one `mogg.call`; the shape/tensor
// reconstruction + `mogg.call.opaque` move into the MAP-ABI stub.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @one_plain
// CHECK: mogg.routine (%{{.*}} : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB0:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.context
// CHECK-NOT: mogg.call.opaque
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB0]] private (%{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.context) attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   %[[ISH:.*]] = mogg.shape.create() {{.*}}{{$}}
// CHECK:   %[[IT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %[[ISH]]) {{.*}}mut = false{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   %[[OT:.*]] = mogg.tensor.create(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) {{.*}}mut = true{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOnePlainOutput inputs(%[[IT]] : !mogg.tensor) outputs(%[[OT]] : !mogg.tensor) context(%{{.*}} : !mogg.context)
// CHECK:   mogg.output
mo.graph @one_plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Fused output: the epilogue lambda + `mogg.tensor.create.epilogue` ride inside
// the stub body alongside the call.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @one_fused
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]]) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB1:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.context
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB1]] private {{.*}} attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   %{{.*}} = mogg.tensor.create.epilogue %{{.*}} (%{{.*}} : !mogg.simd<f32>, %{{.*}} : !map.index<2>) capturing {%[[CAP:[^ ,)]+]] = %{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor} ptr %{{.*}} {{.*}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.tensor.store %[[CAP]][%{{.*}}] = %{{.*}}
// CHECK:   }
// CHECK:   mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerOneFusedOutput
// CHECK:   mogg.output
mo.graph @one_fused(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_fused_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// Dynamic dim: the `!mogg.dim` block arg is forwarded through the call.stub into
// the stub signature, where `mogg.shape.create` consumes it.
// CHECK-LABEL: mo.graph @dyn
// CHECK:   inputs (%[[IP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   outputs (%[[OP:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   context (%[[C:[^ ,)]+]])
// CHECK:   dims (%[[D:.*]]: !mogg.dim<batch>) attributes {device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>, fusionInfo = {{.*}}} {
// CHECK:     mogg.call @[[STUB2:__[A-Za-z0-9_]+]] %[[IP]], %[[OP]], %[[D]], %[[C]] : !mogg.pointer, !mogg.pointer, !mogg.dim<batch>, !mogg.context
// CHECK: mogg.func @[[STUB2]] private (%{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %{{.*}}: !mogg.pointer, %[[SD:.*]]: !mogg.dim<batch>, %{{.*}}: !mogg.context) attributes {abi = #mogg.abi<MOGG>,
// CHECK:   mogg.shape.create(%[[SD]]) {{.*}} : !mogg.dim<batch>
mo.graph @dyn(%a: !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_one_plain_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[batch, 4], f32>
}

GraphCompiler/test/mo-opt/MOGGDialect/Transforms/package.mlir · complete source
// RUN: mo-opt %s --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" --mogg-conform-call-operands | FileCheck %s

// ConformCallOperands runs directly on the mogg codegen ops (the
// post-MAPToMOGG form, with plain !mogg.tensor operands). It re-runs operand
// inference against the callee mogg.kernel.decl and materializes the non-tensor
// operands the kernel expects: a scalar operand is wrapped in
// mogg.scalar.create, and a run of variadic tensor operands is packed into one
// mogg.tuple.create.

// The second input is a scalar kernel argument.
// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @scalar
// CHECK: %[[SC:.*]] = mogg.scalar.create(%{{.*}})
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerScalar inputs(%{{.*}}, %[[SC]] : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.scalar) outputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) context(%{{.*}} : !mogg.context)
func.func @scalar(%in: !mogg.tensor, %scalar: !mogg.tensor, %out: !mogg.tensor, %ctx: !mogg.context) {
  mogg.call.opaque @testing_kernels.testing_kernels.MapLowerScalar inputs(%in, %scalar : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor) outputs(%out : !mogg.tensor) context(%ctx : !mogg.context)
  return
}

// The two inputs satisfy one variadic kernel argument.
// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @variadic
// CHECK: %[[TUP:.*]] = mogg.tuple.create(%{{.*}}, %{{.*}}) : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerVariadic inputs(%[[TUP]] : !mogg.tuple) outputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) context(%{{.*}} : !mogg.context)
func.func @variadic(%a: !mogg.tensor, %b: !mogg.tensor, %out: !mogg.tensor, %ctx: !mogg.context) {
  mogg.call.opaque @testing_kernels.testing_kernels.MapLowerVariadic inputs(%a, %b : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor) outputs(%out : !mogg.tensor) context(%ctx : !mogg.context)
  return
}

// Repacking rebuilds the call, so it has to carry the epilogue flag over. Emit
// reads it instead of inspecting an output's producer, and packing is what
// replaces that producer -- dropping it silently disables the epilogue.
// CHECK-LABEL: func.func @variadicKeepsEpilogueFlag
// CHECK: mogg.call.opaque @{{.*}}MapLowerVariadic inputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tuple) outputs(%{{.*}} : !mogg.tensor) context(%{{.*}} : !mogg.context) hasEpilogueFusion = true
func.func @variadicKeepsEpilogueFlag(%a: !mogg.tensor, %b: !mogg.tensor, %out: !mogg.tensor, %ctx: !mogg.context) {
  mogg.call.opaque @testing_kernels.testing_kernels.MapLowerVariadic inputs(%a, %b : !mogg.tensor, !mogg.tensor) outputs(%out : !mogg.tensor) context(%ctx : !mogg.context) hasEpilogueFusion = true
  return
}

// RUN: rm -rf %t && mkdir -p %t
// RUN: env MODULAR_DEBUG=ir-output-dir=%t mo-opt %s \
// RUN:   --mogg-import-packages="mojo-pkg-paths=%kernel_api_test_lib" \
// RUN:   --mo-to-map --map-fuse-kernels --map-allocate-accumulating-buffers \
// RUN:   --map-outline-structured-kernel-bodies \
// RUN:   --canonicalize --cse --map-to-mogg \
// RUN:   --mogg-conform-call-operands \
// RUN:   --mogg-outline-routines --mogg-to-mgp --mogg-emit-mojo \
// RUN:   -verify-each=false
// RUN: cat %t/*.mojo | FileCheck %s

// End-to-end MAP-ABI emission of the three variadic packing ABIs. The
// `$variadic_abi` attribute `ConformCallOperands` stamps on
// `mogg.tuple.create` (from the callee's variadic parameter type) selects the
// aggregate `TupleCreateOp::emitMojo` builds, so emission never inspects the
// producing ops.

// FUSED INPUT: mo.concat's variadic inputs are fused, so they pack into a
// `_FusedInputVariadicTensors` carrying a per-element `_FusionPack`.
// CHECK: managed_tensor_slice._FusedInputVariadicTensors[
mo.graph @fused_input(%a: !mo.tensor<[2], si32>, %b: !mo.tensor<[3], si32>, %c: !mo.tensor<[4], si32>) -> !mo.tensor<[9], si32> {
  %result = mo.concat[0](%a, %b, %c) : (
    !mo.tensor<[2], si32>, !mo.tensor<[3], si32>, !mo.tensor<[4], si32>
  ) -> !mo.tensor<[9], si32>
  mo.output %result : !mo.tensor<[9], si32>
}

// FUSED OUTPUT: the kernel's variadic outputs are store-epilogue-fused, so they
// pack into a `_FusedOutputVariadicTensors`.
// CHECK: managed_tensor_slice._FusedOutputVariadicTensors[
mo.graph @fused_output(%a: !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) {
  %c:2 = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_variadic_fused_output", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a) : (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>) -> (!mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>)
  mo.output %c#0, %c#1 : !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>, !mo.tensor<[2, 2], f32>
}

// PLAIN: an unfused variadic input packs into a plain `VariadicTensors`.
// CHECK: extensibility.VariadicTensors[
mo.graph @plain(%a: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>, %b: !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32> {
  %c = mo.custom [symbol = "map_lower_variadic", device = #M.device_ref<"cpu", 0>](%a, %b) : (!mo.tensor<[4], f32>, !mo.tensor<[4], f32>) -> !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
  mo.output %c : !mo.tensor<[4], f32>
}

from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
from max.driver import CPU, Accelerator, Buffer, accelerator_count
from max.dtype import DType
from max.engine.api import InferenceSession
from max.graph import DeviceRef, Graph, TensorType, ops


def main() -> None:
    mojo_kernels = Path(__file__).parent / "kernels"

    dtype = DType.float32

    # Place the graph on a GPU, if available. Fall back to CPU if not.
    device = CPU() if accelerator_count() == 0 else Accelerator()
    if accelerator_count() == 0:
        N = 8
        D = 8
        BD = 4
        BN = 4
    else:
        N = 32
        D = 32
        BD = 8
        BN = 16

    with Graph(
        "fused_attention",
        input_types=[
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
            TensorType(
                dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
            ),
        ],
        custom_extensions=[mojo_kernels],
    ) as graph:
        q, k, v, *_ = graph.inputs
        results = ops.custom(
            name="modular_ops::fused_attention_custom",
            device=DeviceRef.from_device(device),
            parameters={"BD": BD, "BN": BN},
            values=[q, k, v],
            out_types=[
                TensorType(
                    dtype, shape=[N, D], device=DeviceRef.from_device(device)
                )
            ],
        )
        graph.output(*results)

    # Set up an inference session for running the graph.
    session = InferenceSession(devices=[device])

    # Compile the graph.
    compiled = session.compile(graph)
    model = session.init(compiled)

    np.random.seed(123)
    Q = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    K = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)
    V = Buffer.from_numpy(np.random.randn(N, D).astype("f")).to(device)

    output = model.execute(Q, K, V)
    print(output)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""
The code below computes the attention score for a tile of size BN x BD.
It follows the exact arithmetic as described in the FlashAttention-2 paper
(https://arxiv.org/pdf/2307.08691). The variable names in this program
reflect the variable names in the algorithms from the paper.

Here, the following tensors are Q for the query,
K for the key, V for the value, and O for the output.

       Q            K               V
  +----D----+  +----D----+   +--+--BD--+---+
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  BN........|  N.........|   N  |......|   |
  |.........|  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  |         |  |.........|   |  |......|   |
  +---------+  +---------+   +--+------+---+

The main trick is in the softmax computation.
As the paper says, S and P are intermediate values.

Let S = Q * K^T  ∈ R^{N, D}
    P = Softmax(S) ∈ R^{N, D}
The attention score is O = P * V ∈ R^{N, D}.

One way to think about this is to consider what happens if we
split the dimensions N in  K, and Q into two tiles: K_1 and K_2, V_1 and V_2.
Then we can incrementally compute the output as follows:
  S_1 = Q * K_1, S_2 = Q * K_2
  O_i = O_{i-1} * renormalization_factor + softmax(S_i) * V_i

This allows for the incremental computation of softmax(S_i) * V_i,
leading to the final output.
"""


from max.gpu.host import DeviceContext
from max.gpu import block_idx
from max.gpu.sync import barrier
from layout import TensorLayout, TileTensor, row_major, stack_allocation
from layout.math import max, sum
from layout.tensor_core import TensorCore

from extensibility import register, InputTensor, OutputTensor

from std.utils import Index


@register("modular_ops::fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttention:
    """Registers the `fused_attention_custom` op, allowing python to use it from the `max`
    package.
    """

    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        comptime assert rank == 2, "rank must be 2"

        # Query tensor
        var Q = query.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Key tensor
        var K = key.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Value tensor
        var V = value.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()
        # Attention output tensor
        var O = output.to_tile_tensor().as_unsafe_any_origin()

        comptime if target == "cpu":
            print("Running on CPU")
            fused_attention_cpu[BN, BD](Q, K, V, O)
        else:
            var dev_ctx = ctx
            print("Running on GPU")
            fused_attention_gpu[BN, BD](dev_ctx, Q, K, V, O)


# CustomOpLibrary does not support names with '::' in them currently. Create
# a simple alias so the whisper example works.
@register("fused_attention_custom")
struct FusedAttentionAlias:
    @staticmethod
    def execute[
        dtype: DType,
        rank: Int,
        //,  # Forces the previous two params to be inferred from the args
        BN: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split Q into
        BD: Int,  # Dimension of blocks to split K, V into
        target: StaticString,  # "cpu" or "gpu"
    ](
        output: OutputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        query: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        key: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        value: InputTensor[dtype=dtype, rank=rank, ...],
        ctx: DeviceContext,
    ) raises:
        FusedAttention.execute[BN=BN, BD=BD, target=target](
            output, query, key, value, ctx
        )


@inline(.always)
def matmul_b_transpose(
    lhs: TileTensor,
    rhs: TileTensor,
    out res: TileTensor[
        lhs.dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[lhs.dtype](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
        comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[0]):
            res[m, n] = 0.0

            comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                    lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[n, k].cast[res.dtype]())


# The bulk of the code below implements what the papers calls
# an "online softmax", which is local to each block.
# The algorithm is described as:
#
# $$$
# m_1 = rowmax(S_1)
# l_1 = rowsum(e^(S_1-m_1))
# P_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1)
# O_1 = P_1*V_1 = diag(l_1)^-1 * e^(S_1-m_1) * V_1
# m_2 = max(m_1, rowmax(S_2)) = m
# l_2 = e^(m_1-m_2) * l_1 _ rowsum(e^(S_2-m_2))
#     = rowsum(e^(S_1-m)) + rowsum(e^(S_2-m)) = ls
# P_2 = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m_2)
# O_2 = diag(l_1/l_2)^-1 * O_1 + (P_2 * V_2)
#     = diag(l_2)^-1 * e^(S_2-m) * V
# $$$


@inline(.always)
def fused_attention_cpu[
    BN: Int, BD: Int
](Q: TileTensor, K: TileTensor, V: TileTensor, O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],):
    comptime N = K.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = K.static_shape[1]

    comptime for tile_n in range(N // BN):
        var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](tile_n, 0)

        comptime for tile_d in range(D // BD):
            var m_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
                Scalar[Q.dtype].MIN
            )

            var l_1 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)

            var O_i = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

            comptime for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN):
                var K_tile = K.tile[BN, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
                var V_tile = V.tile[BN, BD](tile_n_idx, tile_d)

                var S = matmul_b_transpose(Q_tile, K_tile)
                var m_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                max[axis=1](S, m_2)
                m_2.max(m_1)

                # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
                var l_2 = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                l_2.copy_from(m_1)
                l_2 -= m_2
                l_2.exp()
                l_2 *= l_1
                var E = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN, BN]())
                E.copy_from(S)
                E -= m_2
                E.exp()
                var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
                l_2 += l_2_sum

                # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
                E /= l_2
                O_i *= l_1
                O_i /= l_2
                var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[Q.dtype](row_major[BN]())
                m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
                m_1_delta -= m_2
                m_1_delta.exp()
                O_i *= m_1_delta
                var PV = matmul["cpu"](E, V_tile)
                O_i += PV
                m_1.copy_from(m_2)
                l_1.copy_from(l_2)

            O.tile[BN, BD](tile_n, tile_d).copy_from(O_i)


@inline(.always)
def matmul[
    dtype: DType,
    rhs_dtype: DType,
    //,
    target: StaticString,
    transpose_b: Bool = False,
](
    lhs: TileTensor[dtype, ...],
    rhs: TileTensor[rhs_dtype, ...],
    out res: TileTensor[
        dtype,
        type_of(row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()),
        MutUntrackedOrigin,
        address_space=lhs.address_space,
    ],
):
    res = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=lhs.address_space](
        row_major[lhs.static_shape[0], rhs.static_shape[0]]()
    )

    comptime if target == "cpu":
        comptime for m in range(lhs.static_shape[0]):
            comptime for n in range(rhs.static_shape[1]):
                res[m, n] = 0.0

                comptime for k in range(lhs.static_shape[1]):
                    res[m, n] += rebind[res.ElementType](
                        lhs[m, k].cast[res.dtype]()
                    ) * rebind[res.ElementType](rhs[k, n].cast[res.dtype]())
    else:
        comptime M = lhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime N = rhs.static_shape[0]
        comptime K = lhs.static_shape[1]

        var out_sram = stack_allocation[res.dtype, address_space=.SHARED](
            row_major[M, N]()
        )

        comptime BK = 8

        comptime assert K % 8 == 0, "K needs to be a multiple of 8"

        var mma_b_t = TensorCore[dtype, dtype, Index(M, N, BK), transpose_b]()

        var c_reg = stack_allocation[dtype, address_space=.LOCAL](
            mma_b_t.c_fragment_layout
        ).fill(0)

        # `TensorCore`'s native loads require matching operand dtypes;
        # rebind the B view once when `rhs` carries a different dtype.
        var rhs_typed = rebind[
            TileTensor[
                dtype,
                rhs.LayoutType,
                rhs.origin,
                Engine=rhs.Engine,
                address_space=rhs.address_space,
                linear_idx_type=rhs.linear_idx_type,
            ]
        ](rhs)

        comptime for k_i in range(K // BK):
            var a_reg = mma_b_t.load_a(lhs.tile[M, BK](0, k_i))

            var b_reg = mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[BK, N](k_i, 0))

            comptime if transpose_b:
                b_reg = rebind[type_of(b_reg)](
                    mma_b_t.load_b(rhs_typed.tile[N, BK](0, k_i))
                )

            var d_reg = mma_b_t.mma_op(a_reg, b_reg, c_reg)
            c_reg.copy_from(d_reg)
        mma_b_t.store_d(out_sram, c_reg)

        barrier()
        res.copy_from(out_sram)


def fused_attention_kernel[
    q_dtype: DType,
    q_layout: TensorLayout,
    k_dtype: DType,
    k_layout: TensorLayout,
    v_dtype: DType,
    v_layout: TensorLayout,
    o_dtype: DType,
    o_layout: TensorLayout,
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    Q: TileTensor[q_dtype, q_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    K: TileTensor[k_dtype, k_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    V: TileTensor[v_dtype, v_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
    O: TileTensor[o_dtype, o_layout, MutAnyOrigin],
):
    comptime N = Q.static_shape[0]
    comptime D = Q.static_shape[1]

    var Q_tile = Q.tile[BN, D](block_idx.y, 0)

    var m_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(
        Scalar[q_dtype].MIN
    )
    var l_1 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]()).fill(0)
    var O_i = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BD]()).fill(0)

    comptime BN_1 = 8

    for tile_n_idx in range(N // BN_1):
        var K_tile = K.tile[BN_1, D](tile_n_idx, 0)
        var V_tile = V.tile[BN_1, BD](tile_n_idx, block_idx.x)
        var S = matmul["gpu", transpose_b=True](Q_tile, K_tile)
        var m_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        max[axis=1](S, m_2)
        m_2.max(m_1)

        # l_2 = exp(m_1 - m_2) * l_1 + sum(axis=1, exp(S - m_2))
        var l_2 = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        l_2.copy_from(m_1)
        l_2 -= m_2
        l_2.exp()
        l_2 *= l_1
        var E = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN, BN_1]())
        E.copy_from(S)
        E -= m_2
        E.exp()
        var l_2_sum = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        sum[axis=1](E, l_2_sum)
        l_2 += l_2_sum

        # P = exp(S - m_2) / l_2
        E /= l_2
        O_i *= l_1
        O_i /= l_2
        var m_1_delta = stack_allocation[q_dtype](row_major[BN]())
        m_1_delta.copy_from(m_1)
        m_1_delta -= m_2
        m_1_delta.exp()
        O_i *= m_1_delta
        var PV = matmul["gpu"](E, V_tile)
        O_i += PV
        m_1.copy_from(m_2)
        l_1.copy_from(l_2)
    O.tile[BN, BD](block_idx.y, block_idx.x).copy_from(O_i)


def fused_attention_gpu[
    BN: Int,
    BD: Int,
](
    ctx: DeviceContext,
    Q: TileTensor,
    K: TileTensor,
    V: TileTensor,
    O: TileTensor[mut=True, ...],
) raises:
    comptime kernel_func = fused_attention_kernel[
        Q.dtype,
        Q.LayoutType,
        K.dtype,
        K.LayoutType,
        V.dtype,
        V.LayoutType,
        O.dtype,
        O.LayoutType,
        BN,
        BD,
    ]
    ctx.enqueue_function[kernel_func](
        Q,
        K,
        V,
        O,
        grid_dim=(Int(Q.dim[1]()) // BD, Int(Q.dim[0]()) // BN),
        block_dim=(32),
    )
